articles.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX launches Starship V3 rocket after delays
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX successfully launched its massive Starship V3 rocket on a test flight, marking the largest and most powerful rocket in history. The uncrewed rocket deployed 20 dummy satellites before splashing down in the Indian Ocean after an hour-long journey. Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX, praised the team's achievement while NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman expressed excitement for future missions to the moon and Mars.  The successful test flight, despite engine failures, is expected to boost confidence for investors and NASA as it prepares for future space endeavors.

articles.title: Govt. to move HC on behalf of Dalit families facing eviction - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State government announced it will take legal action to prevent the eviction of seven Dalit families from Paryathukavu settlement near Malayaidamthuruth, Kizhakkambalam.  Minister for Higher Education Roji M. John stated the government would pursue the case in the High Court on Monday and promised to support the residents' decades-long legal battle.

articles.title: Jana Nayagan leak case: Madras High Court denies bail to six accused - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court denied bail to six individuals who shared and watched the leaked film "Jana Nayagan" before its official release.  Justice R. Sakthivel dismissed all bail petitions after the prosecution argued that the illegal viewing of the movie by millions constituted a serious offense.

articles.title: US green card applicants will now have to return to home countries to apply, DHS says | US immigration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: USCIS announced a new policy requiring foreigners seeking green cards to apply for them outside the United States. The move, criticized by aid groups and immigration attorneys, will force many applicants to leave the country while their cases are processed, potentially impacting families and creating further strain on an already burdened system.  The agency cited the need to ensure the integrity of the immigration system and prevent loopholes, but the policy change is expected to have significant consequences for those seeking permanent residency in the US.

articles.title: SpaceX launches its biggest rocket yet in test flight from Texas | SpaceX | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX launched its largest Starship rocket, a redesigned version dubbed V3, on a test flight from Starbase in Texas. The launch carried 20 mock Starlink satellites and marked the company's 12th attempt to fly the vehicle. NASA, which is funding the project, hopes to use the Starship to land astronauts on the moon as part of its Artemis program.  SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has announced plans for an initial public offering of the company.

articles.title: Police drop case against artist who depicted high-profile Australians in uniforms with Nazi symbols | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Michael Agzarian, an artist, was charged with displaying Nazi symbols by a public act without lawful excuse after depicting prominent Australians in military uniforms emblazoned with Nazi symbols.  The charges were dropped before the Downing Centre local court on Friday, almost a year after they were filed. Judge Karen Stafford found that the police had reasonable cause to lay the charges but criticized them for taking seven months to withdraw them. Agzarian's lawyer argued that the artwork was political satire and that his client did not know the symbols were Nazi symbols.

articles.title: Waiting for Green Card? Leave US first, re-enter with an immigrant visa - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has announced new guidance directing immigration officers to require individuals on temporary visas, like B1/B2, F1/M1, J1, H-1B, and O-1, to return to their home countries while they wait for their Green Cards. This policy aims to distinguish between temporary admission and permanent residence, with the USCIS director, Joseph Edlow, stating that individuals seeking lawful permanent residency should apply for immigrant visas through the US Department of State before reentering the United States.

articles.title: Judith Chalmers, presenter of TV series Wish You Were Here, dies aged 90 | Television | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Judith Chalmers, the beloved British TV presenter who hosted Wish You Were Here…? for almost three decades, passed away at 90 after a battle with Alzheimer's disease. Her family said she died peacefully at home surrounded by loved ones.  She began her career in broadcasting at age 13 and went on to host numerous popular programs including Come Dancing and Woman’s Hour. Chalmers was known for her warm, approachable style and iconic sun tan, which became synonymous with the travel show. She is survived by her husband of 58 years, Neil Durden-Smith, and son Mark Durden-Smith, a TV presenter himself.

articles.title: Public hearing for limestone mining called off in Meghalaya after protest - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Jaiñtia National Council, Hima Sutnga Youth Federation, Jaiñtia Students' Union
articles.rephrased_article: The authorities in Meghalaya’s East Jaiñtia Hills district canceled a public hearing for a ₹1,800-crore integrated cement plant and limestone mining project after two groups clashed. Supporters of the project and those opposed to it engaged in violence, including the burning of a truck, leaving several people injured. The conflict followed similar clashes on Thursday near the District Magistrate’s office, where police used batons to disperse the groups.  The Jaiñtia National Council, Hima Sutnga Youth Federation, and Jaiñtia Students’ Union** stormed the public hearing site, leading to its cancellation.

articles.title: Timelapse footage shows giant 'cave' inflated over Paris bridge
articles.rephrased_article: JR, a French artist known for his large-scale art installations, transformed Paris' oldest bridge, the Pont Neuf, overnight into a giant inflatable cave structure called "La Caverne" or "The Cave". The 17th-century landmark was nearly unrecognizable to Parisians until Thursday.  The installation, measuring 120 meters in length and ranging from 12-18 meters in height, will be open to the public starting June 6th and run until June 28th.

articles.title: Chudthebuilder Bond Offer: ChudTheBuilder may be released after reported $1M bond offer from crypto casino “Duel” - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: ChudTheBuilder, whose real name is Dalton Eatherly, may soon be released from jail after a crypto gambling platform called Duel offered to pay his $1 million bond. The news has generated significant online discussion, with many questioning the motivations behind the unusual financial offer in connection with the high-profile case involving serious charges related to a courthouse shooting in Tennessee.  The court has not yet confirmed final approval of the bond payment.

articles.title: Punjab government to remove stray dogs from high footfall public spaces following Supreme Court order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bhagwant Mann, Punjab Chief Minister, announced that the state government will remove stray dogs from all high footfall public spaces as per Supreme Court directions issued on May 19, 2026.  The move aims to ensure public safety and provide relief to citizens concerned about stray dog attacks. The government plans to create adequate shelters for stray dogs while adhering to the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act and ABC Rules regarding euthanasia in cases involving dangerous or rabid animals.

articles.title: ‘Kind of humiliating’: trans community responds to EHRC’s new code of practice | Gender | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Stephen Whittle, a 70-year-old man who advocates for gender recognition, was at the Chelsea flower show when the updated code of practice from the Equality and Human Rights Commission was published. The guidance confirmed that single-sex spaces must be used based on biological sex, leading to mixed reactions. Some welcomed it as a consolidation of last year's court victory, while others expressed concern about its practical implications for trans inclusivity.  Businesses and service providers are grappling with the changes, seeking clarity and time to adapt their policies.

articles.title: San Diego’s Muslims, a mosque, and a city shaken | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The San Diego Muslim community is grieving after an attack that shattered their sense of safety.  The attack has prompted the community to come together and support each other as they try to move forward.

articles.title: 'Go home' for Green Card rule: Immigration attorney Rahul Reddy explains what H-1B visa holders should do now - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The USCIS has issued a new memo that requires individuals seeking Green Cards to apply for visas in their home countries instead of adjusting status within the United States. The memo, which experts say may be challenged in court, emphasizes that approving Green Card applications from within the US is a "favor" and not a right.  The memo's impact on those who have already filed Green Card applications remains unclear, but it suggests individuals with pending I-140 petitions should consult legal counsel to strengthen their case.

articles.title: Judge drops criminal case against Kilmar Abrego Garcia
articles.rephrased_article: A US federal judge dismissed the criminal case against Kilmar Abrego Garcia, who was wrongfully deported to El Salvador last year. The judge ruled that the charges were politically motivated, stating the government only pursued them after Abrego Garcia successfully challenged his removal and the Executive Branch reopened its investigation into a 2022 traffic stop incident.  The justice department has not yet commented on the decision.

articles.title: Danny Go: YouTube star Danny Go mourns heartbreaking loss of 14-year-old son Isaac - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Danny Go, a popular YouTuber known for his family-friendly show "Danny Go!", announced the death of his 14-year-old son, Isaac, who had been battling stage 3 mouth cancer since late 2025.  Go shared a heartfelt tribute on Instagram, expressing his immense love and pride in his son's strength despite facing health challenges. Fans and fellow creators have expressed condolences and support for the family during this difficult time. Go canceled his tour to focus on supporting Isaac and creating special memories with him.

articles.title: Woman sustains injury at Kochi metro worksite - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A young woman was injured in a freak accident when an iron piece from the worksite of Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) fell on her car near Padivattom. The incident occurred during de-shuttering work and caused damage to her windshield.  Afcons Infrastructure, the contractor, has been asked to suspend work until further notice and provide support and compensation to the injured woman. An inquiry will be conducted to determine the cause of the accident and strengthen safety measures.

articles.title: US judge dismisses indictment against Kilmar Abrego Garcia | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A US District Judge dismissed an indictment against Kilmar Abrego Garcia, finding that he would not have been prosecuted if he hadn't challenged his deportation. The judge stated the Department of Justice only reopened its human smuggling probe stemming from a 2022 traffic stop after Abrego Garcia filed his lawsuit.  The case was dismissed due to the timing of the charges, which were seen as retaliatory by the court.

articles.title: From Palestine to Catalonia, Guardiola believed in more than just football | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pep Guardiola, the legendary Manchester City manager, is stepping down after a decade of success.  He has used his platform to advocate for various causes beyond football, including Palestinian children in Gaza and homelessness in the UK. His outspokenness on these issues, while widely praised, also drew criticism from some groups, particularly regarding his comments about the Jewish community. Guardiola's legacy extends far beyond trophies won, as he has consistently used his influence to speak up for social justice.

articles.title: Quote of the day by English physicist Brian Cox: “We explore because we are curious, not because we wish to develop grand views of reality or better widgets.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Brian Cox's quote, "We explore because we are curious, not because we wish to develop grand views of reality or better widgets," highlights the inherent value of curiosity in human exploration.  While modern societies often prioritize practical outcomes and measurable results, history demonstrates that many significant discoveries began without immediate applications. Cox emphasizes that exploration is driven by a desire to understand what is unknown, regardless of potential future benefits. This quote challenges the assumption that all exploration must have an immediate purpose or tangible result.

articles.title: State-sponsored apprenticeships and decriminalising cannabis on the bill at Victoria’s Labor conference | Jacinta Allan | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jacinta Allan, Victorian Premier, will announce a plan to create a government-owned electricity body that will hire electrical apprentices at the Labor party's final state conference before the election. The plan aims to address workforce shortages in the industry and is inspired by her father's experience as a linesman at the State Electricity Commission (SEC).  The conference will also feature discussions on various policy proposals, including reducing workweeks, increasing reproductive health leave, decriminalizing cannabis, and addressing issues like public transport affordability.

articles.title: US judge dismisses criminal indictment against Kilmar Ábrego García | Kilmar Ábrego García | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A US judge dismissed a criminal indictment against Kilmar Ábrego García, finding that the Trump administration would not have prosecuted him had he not challenged his deportation.  Ábrego García, who entered the United States without authorization, became a symbol of the Trump administration's mass deportations after being sent to El Salvador's notorious anti-terrorism prison, Cecot. The White House initially opposed his return but was ordered by the Supreme Court to facilitate it. Ábrego García pleaded not guilty, arguing he was being prosecuted in retaliation for suing the government.

articles.title: Massive, absurd: Immigration experts, foreign-born founder react to new Green Card rule - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: USCIS has issued a memo requiring all visa holders in the US to leave and apply for Green Cards from their home countries. The agency argues that visa holders come to the US temporarily, while Green Cards are for permanent residents, creating a conflict of intent. Nick Davidov, founder of a Russian-origin venture capital firm, criticized the policy, stating it would force top scientists and entrepreneurs to leave the country and wait years for their applications to be processed. Immigration specialist James Blunt echoed these concerns, highlighting that even former First Lady Melania Trump could have been subject to this rule. Legal experts believe the memo is vague and will likely be challenged in court as it deviates from Congress's intent when establishing the H-1B visa program.

articles.title: Bowring Hospital wall collapse: Lokayukta probe finds major safety lapses - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Lokayukta inquiry into the fatal wall collapse at the Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital in Shivajinagar, Karnataka, has revealed multiple structural and administrative failures. The investigation found that the wall was constructed beyond permissible height limits, had been damaged previously, and lacked proper drainage systems and retaining walls.  The inquiry also highlighted negligence by authorities who failed to monitor dangerous structures and encroachments. Senior IAS and IPS officers, officials from various departments, and hospital authorities appeared before the Lokayukta for questioning. The Lokayukta directed authorities to identify similar unsafe structures and take preventive measures.

articles.title: US spy chief Tulsi Gabbard resigns under pressure from White House: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, the US Director of National Intelligence, resigned from her position to support her husband, who has been diagnosed with an extremely rare form of bone cancer.  She informed President Donald Trump of her decision during a meeting in the Oval Office on Friday and plans to leave her post on June 30th. Gabbard acknowledged progress made at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, but stated that there is still important work to be done before her departure.

articles.title: 'I can not in good conscience...': What Tulsi Gabbard wrote about her husband in her resignation letter - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, the Director of National Intelligence, submitted her resignation, effective June 30, 2026.  She cited her husband's recent diagnosis with a rare form of bone cancer as the reason for her departure. Gabbard stated that she needed to step away from her duties to support her husband and ensure he could face his illness alone. Joe Kent, Gabbard's deputy, resigned in March.

articles.title: Waymo pauses robotaxis in four Texas cities and Atlanta over flooded road risk
articles.rephrased_article: Waymo has paused its robotaxi service in five US cities, including Atlanta and San Antonio, due to a software issue that has led some vehicles to drive into flooded roads. The company issued a recall of nearly 3,800 robotaxis after an incident on April 20th in San Antonio, Texas. Waymo stated it is working on additional software safeguards and expects to resume service soon.  The company also temporarily suspended its service on freeways in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Phoenix, and Miami while evaluating its cars' performance in construction zones.

articles.title: Nobel Prize winner Olga Tokarczuk under fire after revealing she uses AI to develop ideas | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Olga Tokarczuk, the 2018 Nobel Prize winner in Literature, sparked controversy after remarks at Impact’26 in Poznań where she discussed using AI for brainstorming and research. While acknowledging the potential of AI to enhance creativity, she clarified that her upcoming novel was not written with AI and primarily uses it for fact-checking.  Her comments drew criticism from some Polish writers who saw them as an endorsement of AI-written fiction, but she later issued a clarification stating she uses AI as a tool to support traditional writing practices. The debate surrounding Tokarczuk's remarks highlights the ongoing discussion about the role of AI in artistic creation and its impact on authorship.

articles.title: Australian man dies after falling down ravine on hike to Machu Picchu
articles.rephrased_article: A 52-year-old Australian man, Matthew Cameron Paton, died after falling down a ravine while hiking the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu in Peru. Paton was reported missing on Wednesday after he fell through a broken railing while with a group of tourists and a guide.  His body was found by members of the High Mountain Rescue Unit in Cusco. Authorities are investigating the cause of the fall, and Paton's family described him as a devoted husband and father who had always wanted to travel to Peru.

articles.title: Carlo Petrini, Slow Food movement founder, dies aged 76 | Italy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Carlo Petrini, the founder of the Slow Food movement, has died at age 76.  He led the organization, which promotes sustainable and local cuisine since its inception in 1986, until 2022. President Sergio Mattarella and Italian agriculture minister Francesco Lollobrigida both expressed their condolences, highlighting Petrini's impact on food culture and sustainability. The movement has grown to be active in over 160 countries, including a significant presence in Britain where it was supported by King Charles.  Petrini's legacy will continue through the global Slow Food movement he helped create.

articles.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX postpones Starship launch as mega share sale looms
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX has postponed its Starship launch due to a malfunctioning hydraulic pin on the launch tower, with an attempt scheduled for Friday. The delay comes ahead of SpaceX's record-breaking IPO on the Nasdaq stock market, which could make Elon Musk, already the world's richest person, the first trillionaire.  The uncrewed launch will mark the debut of Starship V3, a powerful rocket designed to carry 100 metric tons and support future missions.

articles.title: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto inaugurates 39km-long Shahrah-i-Bhutto linking Qayyumabad to M9 Motorway - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari inaugurated the 39-kilometer Shahrah-i-Bhutto Expressway, linking Karachi's Qayyumabad to the M-9 Motorway.  He also laid the foundation stone for a new expressway project connecting Karachi Port to Qayyumabad. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah highlighted the expressway's six interchanges, lanes, and elevated section, emphasizing its potential to reduce travel time by an hour. Bilawal Bhutto Zardari emphasized the PPP's commitment to public-private partnerships in developing Karachi and Pakistan, citing projects worth billions of rupees underway. He also announced plans for a Sindh International Financial Centre and a defense production zone in Karachi.

articles.title: Slow Food founder Carlo Petrini dies aged 76 in Italy
articles.rephrased_article: Carlo Petrini, founder of the Slow Food movement, passed away at age 76 in his Italian hometown.  He established the organization in response to protests against the opening of the first McDonald's in Italy and led it for decades, promoting sustainable food production and traditional cooking practices. His work connected communities worldwide and earned him friendships with figures like King Charles III and Pope Francis. The movement emphasizes quality, environmental sustainability, and fair conditions for producers.

articles.title: Kim Soo-hyun: AI used to fake evidence that ended South Korean actor's career, say police
articles.rephrased_article: South Korean police are seeking an arrest warrant for a YouTuber, Kim Se-ui, who allegedly faked evidence to defame actor Kim Soo-hyun. The YouTuber manipulated screenshots of text messages and shared an audio file made with AI to falsely portray the actor as having dated actress Kim Sae-ron when she was underage.  The allegations led to Kim Soo-hyun's career downfall, prompting him to seek legal action against the YouTuber and the actress' family.

articles.title: How a failed attempt to protect a tablecloth led to Jacques E. Brandenberger’s invention of “cellophane” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jacques E. Brandenberger, a Swiss inventor born in 1872, accidentally discovered Cellophane while trying to create stain-resistant fabric.  Inspired by observing wine being spilled on a tablecloth, he developed a flexible cellulose film that became widely used in food packaging and consumer goods due to its transparency and protective qualities. The invention revolutionized retail packing, offering consumers the ability to view products before purchase, and paved the way for modern transparent packaging. Cellophane, while initially intended for textiles, has become a symbol of modernity and hygiene, with its biodegradability making it an attractive alternative to single-use plastics in today's market.

articles.title: In 2002, cavers found a hidden skeleton that revealed an ancient Australian predator | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A group of cavers discovered the bones of a marsupial lion, an extinct apex predator, in a limestone cave on the Nullarbor Plain of southern Australia. The discovery was made possible by the cave's stable environment, which has preserved the fossil for millions of years due to its lack of air movement and limited water penetration.  The findings offer a unique glimpse into the extinct ecosystem of the continent and provide valuable insights into the bone density, predatory biting power, and climbing mechanics of the marsupial lion.

articles.title: IHC bans killing of stray dogs, orders authorities to implement humane methods of population control - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has banned the killing of stray dogs in the federal capital, ordering authorities to implement a humane population control program. The court ruled that mass killing of animals is not consistent with Islamic law or international principles and directed the Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad, the Capital Development Authority (CDA), and other relevant bodies to ensure no inhumane actions are taken against stray dogs.  The court also ordered the creation of an advisory committee, a dog bite database, and improved waste management in residential and commercial areas.

articles.title: Donald Trump: 'If I do attend, I get killed': Donald Trump says he 'has a thing called Iran' stopping him from attending son's wedding - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump suggested he may skip his eldest son Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding in the Bahamas due to escalating tensions with Iran.  Trump stated that attending would likely result in negative media attention and potential harm, while not attending could also lead to criticism. The wedding is a private ceremony with only close family members and friends invited.

articles.title: Greek Philosopher Epicurus: Quote of the day by Greek philosopher Epicurus: “You don't develop courage by being happy in your relationships everyday. You develop it by…” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Epicurus, a Greek philosopher, believed that courage is not developed through easy times but rather through facing and overcoming difficult experiences.  His quote emphasizes that people often discover resilience and strength during challenging periods, even if they don't recognize these changes while they are happening. While happiness and comfort can be important aspects of life, Epicurus argued that true fulfillment comes from navigating uncertainty and hardship, which ultimately lead to personal growth and development.

articles.title: Indigenous Vayu Astra-1 completes high-altitude trials in Uttarakhand, Pokhran - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nibe Limited, a Pune-based defense technology firm, successfully completed no-cost, no-commitment demonstrations of its indigenous loitering munition system ‘Vayu Astra-1’ for the Indian Army. The demonstrations were conducted in April at Pokhran in Rajasthan and Joshimath (Malari) in Uttarakhand.  The anti-personnel variant of Vayu Astra-1 demonstrated a 10-kg warhead strike at a range of 100 km with a CEP of less than one meter, achieving an abort attack and reattack capability during the trials.

articles.title: "She is going to end up in jail again": Asmongold fires back after Nina Lin blames him for spending night in jail over $4 scissors - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nina Lin and Asmongold engaged in a heated online dispute after Lin accused Asmongold of being involved in a situation that led to her spending the night in jail.  Lin claimed she accidentally failed to scan a pair of scissors at a self-checkout counter, leading to police involvement. Asmongold, who was shown clips of the incident during his livestream, responded by calling Lin's accusations baseless and predicting further trouble for her. The exchange has sparked widespread debate within Twitch, Kick, and X communities.

articles.title: GCDA market revamp spells tough times for traders ahead of monsoon - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA) market vendors in Kadavanthra are facing hardship due to delayed renovation works.  The project, aimed at replacing floor tiles and improving the roof, is expected to be completed before the monsoon season arrives next week. V.G. Vincent, a fish vendor, expressed concern about the impact of the upcoming monsoon on his business.

articles.title: Lupita Nyong’o responds to rightwing criticism of The Odyssey: ‘Our cast is representative of the world’ | Lupita Nyong'o | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Lupita Nyong’o, Oscar-winning actress, defended her casting in Christopher Nolan's adaptation of The Odyssey, stating that the film's diverse cast reflects the world. She acknowledged criticisms from figures like Elon Musk, who accused Nolan of making a "DEI" hire for awards, but emphasized that she supports his vision and believes the cast is representative.  Nyong’o also addressed her experiences with casting roles following her Oscar win, noting the prevalence of enslaved women's roles offered to her.

articles.title: Trump says he will ‘try and make’ son’s wedding, but timing is ‘not good’ for him | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump expressed uncertainty about attending his son Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding in the Bahamas over Memorial Day weekend, citing a full schedule of work, including the ongoing war in Iran.  He acknowledged that he might attend but admitted it would be a "small little private affair." The president has been facing declining approval ratings and is reportedly concerned about appearing out of touch with the public's financial struggles.

articles.title: Manipur DGP moved to Cabinet Secretariat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajiv Singh, a 1993 batch Indian Police Service (IPS) officer of Tripura cadre, has been appointed Secretary (Security) in the Cabinet Secretariat.  He was appointed as Manipur's police chief in June 2023 following ethnic violence between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo people. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approved his appointment on Thursday, May 21, 2026. Singh oversaw the recovery of over 4,500 weapons looted from police armouries after the May 2023 violence and led efforts to arrest around 1,000 extortionists during Manipur's state of President's Rule.

articles.title: Single-sex toilets must exclude transgender people, says EHRC | Gender | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) has released a new code of practice for public bodies, businesses, and service providers in England, Wales, and Scotland regarding single-sex facilities. The guidance clarifies that while services must adhere to the supreme court's ruling on sex in the Equality Act 2010, they can offer alternative options like gender-neutral toilets for those who do not wish to use services based on their biological sex.  The document acknowledges potential negative impacts on transgender individuals and encourages a broader conversation about inclusive access to facilities. However, it also emphasizes that excluding trans people from single-sex facilities is not proportionate in healthcare settings where mixed-sex accommodation is unavailable. The code remains in draft form and will be finalized after 40 days of parliamentary review.

articles.title: Zohran Mamdani: Zohran Mamdani enters streamer era with live Twitch series “Talk with the People” - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Zohran Mamdani, the mayor of New York City, is launching a new livestream show called "Talk with the People" on Twitch. The first stream will take place on May 21 at 4 PM ET and will feature Mamdani answering questions from viewers about city issues and daily life in NYC.  The show will also be available on YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, X, and Bluesky, but the main platform for direct interaction is Twitch. The aim of the series is to connect younger generations with City Hall by creating a more accessible and understandable dialogue between government officials and citizens.

articles.title: Guardian journalists win across categories at Press Awards in London | Newspapers & magazines | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Guardian won several awards at the Press Awards in London, including Political Journalist of the Year for Pippa Crerar, Broadsheet Feature Writer of the Year for Simon Hattenstone, and Young Journalist of the Year for Malak A Tantesh.  Her reporting from besieged Gaza provided a vital perspective during a time when international journalists were largely barred. The Guardian's podcast team also took home News Podcast of the Year for their investigation into the disappearance of British journalist Dom Phillips and Brazilian indigenous expert Bruno Pereira, while The Times won Daily Newspaper of the Year.

articles.title: New govt. hospital, preventing waterlogging are among my priorities, says Katpadi MLA - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Sudhakar, Katpadi MLA, has identified traffic congestion between the railway station and Green Circle roundabout as a top priority for his constituency. He proposes diverting trucks and goods lorries from Andhra Pradesh to reach Ranipet and Kancheepuram via Chittoor limits, aiming to alleviate the heavy traffic flow during rush hour on Old Katpadi Road.  He plans to present this proposal to the State government.

articles.title: Domestic abuse law fails to recognise danger of tech abuse, Lords committee told | Online abuse | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Lords select committee heard that the Domestic Abuse Act 2021, while encompassing physical and psychological abuse, does not fully address technology-facilitated abuse.  Jen Reed, head of policy at University College London’s Gender and Tech Research Lab, emphasized that tech abuse is as devastating as physical abuse, citing examples like stalkerware and AirTags used for tracking. Kaspersky reported 45% of respondents globally experienced tech abuse in the past year. While tech abuse was included in statutory guidance, Reed argued it's often treated as an online safety issue rather than a core aspect of domestic abuse.

articles.title: Radio station mistakenly announces death of King Charles - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Radio Caroline, a former British pirate radio station, apologized for announcing the death of King Charles III on Tuesday afternoon due to a computer error. The station's manager, Peter Moore, stated that the error triggered a "death of a monarch" procedure and led to an on-air apology.  Moore also confirmed that the station plans to continue broadcasting the King's Christmas message in the future.

articles.title: 'At least 3 fewer Indians': Woman's post on Meta layoff affecting H-1B visa holder with wife and kid in Seattle draws flak - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A viral social media post highlighted the impact of Meta's recent layoffs on Indian workers abroad, with many users celebrating the job loss and speculating about the man's immigration status. The post suggested that the engineer was in Bengaluru, India, and had a 30-year plan on a 3-year visa, prompting discussions about the risks associated with working on temporary visas in the US. Social media users expressed varying opinions, some criticizing the man's decision to live in the US while on an H-1B visa and others highlighting the potential consequences for his family.

articles.title: Jailed Vietnamese tycoon's Birkin bag sells for nearly £400K
articles.rephrased_article: Two Hermès Birkin bags, confiscated from jailed Vietnamese businesswoman Truong My Lan, sold for over $535,000 at a government auction. The larger bag, a size 25 with rhinestones, fetched nearly seven times its starting bid and the smaller bag, a size 30, sold for less. Nicholas Parnell, founder of Agency Parnell, a wholesale luxury fashion agency, noted that Birkin bags have been increasing in value year-on-year due to their exclusivity and rarity.

articles.title: Three children among seven persons rescued from brick kiln near Arakkonam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Revenue officials rescued seven members of the Irular community from a brick kiln in Minnal village near Arakkonam town. The children, aged 13 to 17, were among those rescued and reported suffering inhumane treatment including physical abuse, long working hours, and inadequate living conditions.  The owner of the brick kiln, K. Palani, and his sons, P. Suresh and P. Suman, are facing legal action. The rescued individuals received release certificates enabling them to access government aid programs for bonded laborers.

articles.title: Quote of the day by physicist Wolfgang Pauli: “I do not mind if you think slowly, but I do object when you publish more quickly than you think.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Wolfgang Pauli, a renowned physicist, famously stated, "I do not mind if you think slowly, but I do object when you publish more quickly than you think."  The quote highlights the importance of thoughtful consideration over hasty conclusions. While speed can be beneficial in certain situations, it should not replace careful thinking and analysis. The quote resonates with modern society's fast-paced culture where instant reactions are often prioritized over genuine understanding.

articles.title: Quote of the day by American astronomer Carl Sagan: “The cosmos is within us. We are made of star-stuff. We are a way for the cosmos to know itself.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Carl Sagan's famous quote, "The cosmos is within us. We are made of star-stuff. We are a way for the cosmos to know itself," highlights the scientific reality that human beings are composed of elements forged in stars billions of years ago. This powerful statement transcends mere science, suggesting that humans are intrinsically connected to the universe and carry a piece of its history within them. Sagan's work aimed to make science accessible and relatable, emphasizing the wonder and curiosity inherent in exploring our place within the vast cosmos.  His words continue to resonate with readers today because they remind us that despite our smallness, we possess an extraordinary ability to question and understand the universe around us.

articles.title: Elon Musk agrees with what Jeff Bezos says on charity: 'If I do my job right...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jeff Bezos, founder of Amazon, stated in an interview that his businesses provide more societal benefit than his charitable donations.  He cited examples like Amazon's essential services during the pandemic and letters from grateful customers as evidence. Elon Musk shared this sentiment, highlighting the value created by for-profit companies. Social media users debated whether Bezos' statement was genuine or a convenient justification for prioritizing profit over philanthropy.

articles.title: Grammacrackers: 81-year-old Minecraft streamer GrammaCrackers swatted during cancer fundraiser stream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sue Jacquot, better known as GrammaCrackers, a 81-year-old Twitch streamer, was swatted during a Minecraft livestream to raise money for her grandson's cancer treatment.  The incident involved multiple police vehicles and officers who entered her home while she was asleep. Despite the frightening experience, GrammaCrackers remained positive, joking about meeting a "pretty policewoman" and expressing gratitude for the support of her family and viewers. The event sparked anger and concern online, with many people expressing their support for the elderly streamer's fundraiser.

articles.title: Mother arrested after boys abandoned by road in Portugal
articles.rephrased_article: Two French boys, aged under five, were found abandoned by the side of a road in Portugal and their mother and stepfather have been arrested. The children were discovered near Alcacer do Sal on Tuesday with backpacks containing food and water but no identification documents.  The boys' father reported them missing from their home in Colmar, France, on May 11th. Police in Portugal and France are investigating the case.

articles.title: Watch: Moment car explodes into massive fireball in NYC
articles.rephrased_article: A hybrid car exploded in Lower Manhattan on Tuesday afternoon, sending thick black smoke and debris into the air. The incident occurred near Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) headquarters and sent people fleeing for safety. Firefighters extinguished the flames after an hour-long response, with no reported injuries.  The cause of the explosion is believed to be an electrical fault.

articles.title: Massive car crash in New Jersey pushes BMW into river; Indian-origin driver arrested after fleeing scene on foot - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A BMW driven by 32-year-old Zorawar S Kohli of Englewood Cliffs crashed into the Hackensack River Bridge on Route 80, causing the vehicle to plunge into the water. The driver escaped and was later found hiding under a train and arrested.  The crash also injured the passenger in the Land Rover, who was taken to a hospital with minor injuries.  State Police investigated the incident, leading to Kohli's arrest on charges of obstruction, resisting arrest, assault by auto, and other motor vehicle offenses.

articles.title: ‘Barring elected representatives, TVK members not to go for inspections’: Minister Arunraj - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) general secretary K.G. Arunraj, Minister for Health and Family Welfare, clarified that only elected representatives are authorized to conduct inspections.  His statement followed criticism of a woman claiming to be from the party's medical wing inspecting the Government Hospital in Sankarankovil, as instructed by TVK president C. Joseph Vijay and general secretary N. Anand.

articles.title: Italian police stop party attended by Mick Jagger over music ban | Mick Jagger | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mick Jagger and other actors from the film "Three Incestuous Sisters" were stopped by police on Stromboli, Italy, for playing music during a Wednesday night celebration. The mayor of Lipari, Riccardo Gullo, enacted a local music ban, which caused confusion but was accepted by the partygoers.  The film crew and actors departed Stromboli on Thursday after the incident, with Jagger leaving via private helicopter.

articles.title: 'Meta reached out to interview me the same week...': US founder asks what happened to employee retention - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Zach Wilson, an American entrepreneur, criticized Meta for its recent layoffs of 8,000 employees following the announcement of a new AI strategy. Wilson expressed his belief that one of those laid-off individuals possesses the necessary qualifications for a principal role offered by Meta.  The company attributed the layoff to "running the company more efficiently" and thanked affected employees for their contributions.

articles.title: Antarvahini Saraswati ‘Antya Pushkaralu’ begins in Kaleshwaram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla and his wife Janaki Shukla participated in religious ceremonies at the Saraswati Ghat during the start of the 12-day ‘Antya Pushkaralu’ festival.  Devotees from across the region gathered to witness the event, which marks the beginning of the sacred celebrations. Sri Shankara Vijayendra Saraswathi Swami of Kanchi Kamakoti Peetam performed special pujas and rituals at the Triveni Sangamam, where the subterranean Antarvahini Saraswati river joins the Godavari and Pranahita rivers.  D. Sridhar Babu, Minister for IT and Industries, and Konda Surekha, Endowments Minister, were also present.

articles.title: Eight cars gutted after carrier truck catches fire on NH-44 in Medak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A container truck carrying new cars caught fire on National Highway 44 near Nagulapally village in Medak district, India.  Police and firefighters battled the blaze for nearly two hours before bringing it under control, preventing any casualties. The fire destroyed eight vehicles inside the truck. Preliminary investigations suggest a mechanical failure may have triggered the incident.

articles.title: Calcutta High Court asks Bengal government to decide on exemption in animal slaughter rules for Eid ul-Adha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Calcutta High Court directed the West Bengal government to decide on an exemption request for animal slaughter during Eid al-Adha, citing Section 12 of the West Bengal Animal Slaughter Control Act, 1950. The court emphasized that a decision should be made within 24 hours of receiving the order, considering the potential festival dates of May 27 or 28.  The petitioners argued for an exemption based on religious practices and claimed the Act's provisions allow for such relaxation, while opposing lawyers maintained that the notification issued on May 13th was in accordance with existing laws and previous court rulings. The court also urged the state to assess its capacity to issue necessary certificates and ensure proper infrastructure for animal slaughter.

articles.title: WiseTech begins redundancies – but omits ‘AI’ from emails to Chinese employees, workers say | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: WiseTech, an Australian Stock Exchange-listed company, is laying off approximately 2,000 employees globally due to advancements in artificial intelligence. The redundancies began in South Korea and Mexico and will continue in other countries including Australia next week.  The company's communication regarding the layoffs has been inconsistent, with internal emails referencing "global transformation" instead of "AI" in some cases. Zubin Appoo, CEO of WiseTech, claims that different legal requirements necessitate varying language across jurisdictions. Employees are expressing concern over the lack of transparency and clarity surrounding the layoff process, leading to low morale and anxiety among those awaiting their fate.

articles.title: I am from India but none of my firm partners is Indian: Attorney Rahul Reddy counters hate on social media - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Reddy, an immigration attorney, and Emily Neumann, a partner at his firm, the Reddy-Neumann Brown PC, addressed concerns about the "Indians only hire Indians" narrative circulating on social media. They emphasized that while fraud exists within the H-1B program, it does not represent the entire process or all individuals involved.  Dr. Sean Wang, a Chinese-American assistant professor, also filed a lawsuit against Southern Methodist University, alleging preferential treatment of Indian employees by head of the department Dr. Hemang Desai.

articles.title: ‘It’s broken English’: MP’s attempt to speak Jamaican in parliament sparks language row | Jamaica | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Jamaican MP, Nekeisha Burchell, sparked controversy in parliament when she spoke in Jamaican Patois during her maiden speech. Juliet Holness, the speaker of the house and wife of Jamaica's prime minister, interrupted her, citing parliamentary rules requiring English language use. The incident ignited debate about the legacy of British colonialism and whether Jamaica should embrace its own language in formal settings.  Marlon Morgan, a parliamentary secretary, argued for a more thoughtful approach to any potential change in language usage within parliament, while others like Carolyn Cooper, a literary scholar, supported Burchell's intervention as a symbol of cultural confidence. The issue has sparked public debate about the legitimacy and use of Jamaican Patois in Jamaica.

articles.title: Jamsetji Tata: Quote of the day by Jamsetji Tata: “Uncommon thinkers reuse what common thinkers refuse.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jamsetji Tata's quote, "Uncommon thinkers reuse what common thinkers refuse," highlights the importance of perspective in recognizing opportunities. The quote emphasizes that uncommon thinkers notice value where others see limitations and often find success by revisiting discarded ideas or overlooked possibilities. This principle applies to various aspects of life, including business, personal growth, and even societal progress. While many people focus on novelty and immediate gratification, Tata's words encourage a more curious approach, suggesting that staying open to different perspectives can lead to unexpected breakthroughs and success.

articles.title: Major fire at hosiery shop in Hyderabad’s Pathergatti - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A major fire broke out at the Younus Hosiery Shop in the SYJ Complex, Pathergatti, Hyderabad on Thursday (May 21, 2026), prompting an extensive emergency response from the Telangana Fire Services Department.  The fire originated in the hosiery shop and spread rapidly within the commercial complex, causing panic among shop owners and nearby establishments.  Firefighters managed to contain the blaze after several hours of firefighting operations, preventing further damage. The cause of the fire is currently under investigation.

articles.title: England Free Bus Travel Scheme: Children across England to get free bus travel this August under £100 million Government Scheme | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chancellor Rachel Reeves announced a new government-backed scheme offering free bus travel for children aged five to 15 throughout England during August. The initiative, part of the "Great British Summer Savings" package, aims to ease pressure on household budgets and is estimated to cost over £100 million. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander stated that the program will allow children unlimited journeys without paying fares or registering in advance.  The scheme applies only to participating local bus operators and excludes long-distance coach services and rail travel.

articles.title: EasyJet summer holiday bookings down on last year amid Iran war uncertainty | easyJet | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: easyJet, the budget airline, reported lagging summer holiday bookings due to consumer uncertainty caused by the Iran war. Kenton Jarvis, easyJet's chief executive, stated that despite fuel price increases and potential disruptions, the airline is well-positioned to manage the current environment and operate normally.  The company has hedged 72% of its fuel needs for the next six months but temporarily suspended short-term hedging due to elevated near-term fuel prices. easyJet also reported a £552m pre-tax loss for the six months to March, compared with a loss of £394m in the same period last year.

articles.title: Candace Owens: "Charlie was about to update his will": Candace Owens sparks backlash after explosive Charlie Kirk conspiracy claims on livestream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens sparked controversy during a recent broadcast with accusations and conspiracy claims surrounding the late Charlie Kirk, his inner circle, and other public figures.  She repeatedly questioned the circumstances of Kirk's death and suggested hidden motives, alleging changes to end-of-life documents and possible monitoring of his communications. Owens also criticized Victor Marx, calling him "unstable" and suggesting a broader effort to divide Christians and Muslims. The episode drew criticism for lacking hard proof and fueling online debates about the validity of her claims.

articles.title: Stray dog euthanasia: Bengaluru examining legally permissible options for ‘rabid, ill, or aggressive dogs’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru’s corporations are grappling with the Supreme Court's ruling that allows for euthanasia of "rabid, incurably ill or demonstrably dangerous" dogs. The court emphasized qualified veterinary assessments and adherence to existing animal welfare laws.  However, a lack of clear guidelines on aggression levels has raised concerns about potential misuse by civic officials. Animal rights activist Arun Prasad warns this could lead to unnecessary dog killings. Meanwhile, Nevina Kamath, a co-petitioner in a previous case regarding stray dog euthanasia, plans to file a review petition against the new ruling.

articles.title: AI will help make a Nobel prize-winning discovery within a year, says Anthropic co-founder | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jack Clark, co-founder of Anthropic, predicts significant advancements in AI within the next few years, including a Nobel Prize-winning discovery and companies run solely by AIs generating millions in revenue. He acknowledges the potential dangers of advanced AI but believes that its development is unstoppable due to fierce competition between countries and commercial interests.  Clark urges humanity to prepare for the transformative power of AI, comparing it to the need for pandemic preparedness. Critics warn that over-reliance on current AI models could lead to "cognitive atrophy" and a weakening of human decision-making.

articles.title: After High Court verdict, Hindu petitioners seek free entry for devotees at Bhojshala in Madhya Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hindu petitioners have filed applications with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and the Union Culture Ministry, demanding free entry to the Bhojshala complex and the removal of "unauthorised Islamic symbols". They also requested that idols of Lord Hanuman and other Hindu deities be retrieved through a scientific excavation. The Madhya Pradesh High Court had declared the site a Vagdevi temple on May 15, quashing an earlier order allowing Muslims to offer namaz there.

articles.title: Nvidia posts record profit of $58.3bn amid AI chip boom | Technology | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nvidia, the chip giant, reported record quarterly profit of $58.3 billion for the February-April period, driven by explosive demand for its advanced AI chips. The company's revenue surged to $81.6 billion, exceeding analysts' estimates and fueled by growth in its data-center business. Nvidia announced a $80 billion stock buyback scheme and a dividend hike, rewarding shareholders. Despite the record results, shares fell slightly after hours, reflecting high expectations for continued growth.

articles.title: Incoming Ofcom chair vows to take on ‘tech bros’ | Ofcom | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ofcom's incoming chair, Ian Cheshire, has pledged to address concerns about the regulator's perceived complacency and slowness in enforcing online safety regulations.  Cheshire emphasized his intention to scrutinize tech companies, particularly social media platforms like TikTok and YouTube, for their efforts to protect children from harmful content. He also acknowledged personal concerns about the impact of social media on under-16s and suggested Ofcom needs to be clear about its limitations in policing these platforms.  Cheshire's comments were welcomed by safety campaigners who believe this signifies a necessary shift towards more robust enforcement.

articles.title: PIL plea filed against deposit of temple funds in State-owned non banking finance corporations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A public interest litigation petition challenging the previous DMK government's decision to deposit temple funds in non-banking finance corporations has been filed in the Madras High Court.  The petitioner, T.R. Ramesh of Indic Collective Trust, argues that these corporations are unsafe and unsuitable for holding temple surplus funds. The court has directed the HR&CE department to file a counter affidavit by May 27th and will hear the case for final hearing next week.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX unveils filing for blockbuster IPO | Elon Musk News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, the rocket technology company founded by Elon Musk, has filed for a blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) that could value it at a record-setting $1.75 trillion.  This would make Musk the first trillionaire in history and cement SpaceX as one of the world's most valuable publicly traded companies. The IPO, expected as early as June 11th, is part of a larger trend of monumental IPOs in the technology sector, including potential offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic.  The sale would allow Musk to pursue ambitious goals like colonizing Mars and building AI data centers in space.

articles.title: Was Nina Lin arrested? Twitch streamer claims missed $4 scissors scan led to night in jail - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nina Lin, a controversial Twitch streamer, claimed she was arrested for failing to scan a pair of scissors worth $4 at a checkout.  She stated the incident occurred during a rushed checkout process and that security footage showed her missing one barcode. Lin has been accused of shoplifting in the past and faces criticism from viewers who believe this latest incident is part of a pattern of behavior. Legal commentator Andre Esquire questioned whether the situation was truly accidental, given Lin's history of similar incidents.

articles.title: Pompeii’s 2,000-year-old mystery jars finally revealed by 3D scans: How Romans built them, and why their function remains a mystery | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists have used 3D scanning technology to study built-in ceramic jars found in Roman taverns at Pompeii, revealing that they were likely made using a controlled, multi-stage process on a potter's wheel. The jars show variations in construction, suggesting multiple workshops or potters were involved. While the jars' original purpose remains unclear, some scholars believe they may have held cooked food due to their fixed location and difficulty in cleaning.

articles.title: Tennessee man jailed for 37 days over Charlie Kirk meme to receive $835,000 settlement - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Larry Bushart, a retired police officer from Tennessee, has settled a lawsuit against local officials for $835,000 after spending 37 days in jail over Facebook posts about the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk.  Bushart was arrested for refusing to remove memes referencing Kirk's death that sparked concern among community members. The Perry County Sheriff and an investigator involved in obtaining the arrest warrant were named as defendants in the lawsuit. Bushart maintains his First Amendment rights were violated, while authorities argued the meme caused fear and hysteria within the community.

articles.title: Tennessee man jailed for 37 days over Charlie Kirk meme to receive $835,000 settlement - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Tennessee man, Larry Bushart, has reached a $835,000 settlement with Perry County officials over his 37-day jail sentence for Facebook posts about the death of conservative activist Charlie Kirk.  Bushart was arrested after authorities deemed his memes concerning Kirk's assassination as causing concern in the community. The case raised concerns about free speech protections and Bushart's lawyer stated that he is pleased his First Amendment rights were vindicated.

articles.title: James Murdoch to acquire New York Magazine and Vox Media Podcast Network | Media News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: James Murdoch, the younger son of media mogul Rupert Murdoch, has acquired New York Magazine and the Vox Media Podcast Network in a deal valued at over $300 million.  The acquisition gives Murdoch control of a storied magazine known for its coverage of culture, politics, and fashion, as well as a podcast division with a reach comparable to cable television news networks. The deal also includes the Vox Media podcast network, which boasts popular programs like "Pivot," and will see Vox Media CEO Jim Bankoff join Lupa Systems, the company owned by Murdoch.

articles.title: Hindu groups perform puja at Bhojshala amid security; ASI issues directions to implement High Court order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hindu Front for Justice, Bhoj Utsav Samiti, and local residents performed Aarti at the Bhojshala complex in Madhya Pradesh's Dhar on Saturday, May 16, 2026. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) acknowledged the High Court's verdict declaring the site a Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Saraswati and a Sanskrit learning center.  The ASI issued an order permitting unrestricted access for the Hindu community while ensuring monument conservation under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958. Muslim representatives have stated they will challenge the decision in the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Mayawati demands extensive relief for storm victims in Uttar Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mayawati, president of the Bahujan Samaj Party, called on the Uttar Pradesh government to provide extensive support to families affected by recent storms and heavy rain that have caused at least 111 deaths. She urged the government to help people rebuild their lives after the destruction of property and loss of life.

articles.title: Body donated for educational purposes cannot be returned: Kerala HC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala High Court ruled that a woman's body, donated to the Government Medical College, Kalamassery, cannot be returned based on her children's request. The court emphasized that the deceased's intention to donate her body for educational purposes overrides any subsequent requests from her children.  As a result, the court dismissed their plea seeking the return of their mother's remains.

articles.title: Harlem Renaissance documentary finally gets global premiere 50 years after cameras rolled | Documentary films | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: William Greaves, a pioneering documentary filmmaker, died in 2014 but his son David and granddaughter Liani are now completing his unfinished film "Once Upon a Time in Harlem."  The documentary, originally shot in 1972, captures the voices of artists, writers, musicians, and organizers from the Harlem Renaissance. The film features conversations about race, language, legacy, and the global reverberations of anti-colonial struggle. David Greaves believes that the film is timely given the current debates surrounding Black history and identity in America.  The film will have its international premiere at Cannes' Directors' Fortnight.

articles.title: Mango Diversity Show at Sangareddy FRC inaugurated - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Nagi Reddy, former Commissioner of Telangana State Election Commission, inaugurated the diamond jubilee celebrations and a two-day 'Mango Diversity Show' at the Fruit Research Station (FRS) in Sangareddy. The event, organized by the Sri Konda Laxman Telangana State Horticultural University (SKLTGHU), featured over 300 mango varieties and demonstrations of agricultural advancements for farmers.  The concluding day will include a 'Mango Processed Products Competition'.

articles.title: North America’s largest commuter rail system shuts down as workers strike | New York | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Long Island Rail Road (LIRR), North America's largest commuter rail system, was shut down on Saturday after five unions representing about half its workforce went on strike.  Janno Lieber, the MTA chairman, stated that the agency cannot accept a deal that would increase fares for riders. The unions are demanding higher wages and healthcare premiums to keep up with inflation and rising living costs. Kathy Hochul, New York's governor, urged both the MTA and the unions to return to negotiations and find a solution.

articles.title: King Charles ‘shocked and saddened’ as soldier dies after falling from horse at Royal Windsor Horse Show
articles.rephrased_article: A member of the King Charles III’s ceremonial artillery unit died following a fall from a horse at the Royal Windsor Horse Show on Friday evening. The soldier, serving with the King’s Troop Royal Horse Artillery, collapsed after leaving the arena and despite receiving immediate medical attention, suffered fatal injuries.  Police are treating the death as “unexplained but not suspicious” while investigations are ongoing in coordination with the Ministry of Defence and event organizers at the Royal Windsor Horse Show.

articles.title: Snorkeling at Pearl Harbor, Philadelphia concert date with girlfriend at $50,000 suite: Kash Patel unfazed by new controversies
articles.rephrased_article: FBI Director Kash Patel defended his recent trips, which included a snorkeling visit to the USS Arizona memorial in Hawaii. Patel was accompanied by nine others on the tour and was told not to touch the sunken ship. The FBI stated that the trip was part of official travel engagements with foreign counterparts.  The agency also confirmed Patel's attendance at a country music concert in Philadelphia with his girlfriend, Alexis Wilkins, who was an invited guest.

articles.title: Mick Jagger and Eric Clapton win battle to stop 29-storey block being built by Thames | Planning policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mick Jagger, Eric Clapton, Felicity Kendal, and Harry Hill successfully opposed a 29-storey tower proposed by Rockwell Property on the banks of the River Thames. The developer's plans, initially for a 34-storey building with 142 flats, were rejected by Wandsworth council and the Greater London Authority due to concerns about its height, scale, and impact on the local area's character. A planning inspector agreed with these objections, concluding that the tower would be "overbearing" and "harmful."  The developer expressed disappointment over the decision but stated they had made changes to the scheme based on public feedback.

articles.title: New USCIS signature rule for H-1B, Green Card: Dos and don'ts for your next immigration application
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Homeland Security has issued an interim rule that expands the authority to reject immigration benefit requests due to signature issues. The rule, effective July 10, 2026, clarifies acceptable signature formats and outlines what constitutes a deficient signature.  Immigration experts warn that even minor signature errors can lead to case delays and potential loss of filing fees. This new rule applies to all individuals seeking immigration benefits under the US framework.

articles.title: Push for public transport exposes structural gaps - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's push for public transport, particularly metro rail, has prompted politicians and bureaucrats to use such systems. However, the renewed spotlight on public transit highlights a gap between policy intent and on-ground delivery.  Years of underinvestment in mass rapid transit systems have led to stalled projects like the Hyderabad Metro’s second phase and the Multi-Modal Transport System (MMTS) network. While efforts are underway to improve connectivity and funding, challenges remain, including securing approvals for expansion and procuring new train sets. The State government is also exploring a Rapid Rail Transit System (RRTS), but its suitability for urban settings remains questioned.

articles.title: Soldier dies after falling from horse at Royal Windsor Horse Show | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A soldier from the King’s Troop, Royal Horse Artillery died after falling from their horse at the Royal Windsor Horse Show on Friday evening.  The incident occurred after a display and despite receiving immediate medical treatment, the soldier was pronounced dead at the scene. Police are investigating the cause of death but consider it to be unexplained. The show is continuing as planned with the omission of the King’s Troop’s display.

articles.title: Kamal meets Vijay, submits 6 demands Tamil film industry’s development - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kamal Haasan, founder of Makkal Needhi Maiam, met with Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to discuss the development of the Tamil film industry.  Haasan presented six demands, including eliminating manual scavenging through technology and establishing village libraries and skill development centers. He also requested the abolition of local body entertain taxes on movie tickets, a strong anti-piracy team, and a state-owned OTT platform for Tamil cinema.

articles.title: 'He couldn’t stop blushing': When Queen Elizabeth II smiled at Prince Harry, his reaction said everything
articles.rephrased_article: A photograph of Queen Elizabeth II smiling at Prince Harry during his military training graduation in 2006 has resurfaced, capturing the warmth of their relationship.  Royal enthusiasts have praised the image for its genuine connection between the Queen and her grandson. The photo is a reminder of the Queen's supportive nature towards her grandchildren, including encouraging them to serve the public. Prince Harry served ten years in the British Army, including two tours to Afghanistan, and founded the Invictus Games to support injured veterans.

articles.title: CJI Surya Kant clarifies ‘parasites’ remarks, says youth are pillars of country - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant issued a statement clarifying that his remarks about "attacks" on institutions were not directed at the youth but at individuals with fake or bogus degrees in professions like law and media. He stated that these individuals act as parasites by attacking institutions without any legitimate standing. The CJI maintained that he holds immense respect for India's youth and expressed pride in their potential to contribute to a developed nation.

articles.title: The surprising reason Joan Kroc’s record-breaking Salvation Army gift still changes lives today
articles.rephrased_article: Joan Kroc's massive donation to the Salvation Army, totaling several billion dollars, resulted in the construction of a network of community centers known as Kroc Centers across the United States.  These centers provide a wide range of services including swimming instruction, fitness classes, youth sports activities, and educational programs, fostering social interaction and community engagement. The donation transformed the Salvation Army's strategy for community engagement by enabling the construction of sustainable facilities that could operate independently from traditional charity events. This tangible legacy has had a lasting impact on communities nationwide.

articles.title: Peacock ‘invasion’ of Italian seaside town ruffles feathers | Italy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Federico Bruni, a resident of Punta Marina, Italy, finds the town's peacock population to be a charming addition.  However, some residents like Francesco and Marco are unhappy with the birds' presence due to their droppings and mating calls disrupting the peace. The peacocks have become increasingly numerous in recent years, likely due to supplementary feeding by locals during the Covid-19 pandemic.  The Ravenna city council is struggling to manage the situation, attempting to find a balance between respecting the birds' natural behavior and maintaining public order.

articles.title: Freight train and bus crash kills at least eight in Bangkok
articles.rephrased_article: An accident involving a freight train and a public bus in Bangkok has resulted in the deaths of at least eight people and injuries to 25 others. The collision, which triggered a fire that engulfed the bus, prompted emergency services to respond with firefighters and rescue crews.  The fire has been contained, but teams continue to search for victims and investigate the cause of the accident.

articles.title: Bhojshala Case: What did the High Court decide? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madhya Pradesh High Court ruled that the Bhojshala-Kamal Maula site is a Hindu temple, granting full worship rights. The verdict has sparked reactions from both sides and may now be appealed to the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Alleged murder of Aboriginal girl highlights Australia's deep inequalities
articles.rephrased_article: The death of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby, an Aboriginal girl from Alice Springs, has sparked national grief and outrage. The circumstances surrounding her alleged murder have brought to light deep inequalities within Australia's child protection system, particularly in remote Aboriginal communities.  Asta Hill, the mayor of Alice Springs, and Catherine Liddle, CEO of SNAICC, a peak body representing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children and their families, have both acknowledged the need for systemic change.  The Northern Territory government has announced a review into its child protection system, but some Aboriginal organizations are critical of this approach, arguing that it could further marginalize already vulnerable communities. Jacinta Nampijinpa Price, Liberal Party Senator, expressed her grief and called for an "honest conversation" about the failures in child protection.  Experts suggest addressing the complex social inequalities that have been present for generations is crucial to preventing similar tragedies from occurring.

articles.title: Reble's Praying Mantis: The female rapper reshaping Indian hip-hop
articles.rephrased_article: Reble, a rapper from Meghalaya, India, has gained significant popularity with her unique blend of English and indigenous languages. Her breakout moment came with the Bollywood film *Dhurandhar*, where her music resonated with audiences.  Her latest single, "Praying Mantis," continues to generate discussion online. Reble's rise reflects a broader shift in Indian pop culture towards embracing regional artists. Despite facing criticism for her style and lyrics, she remains committed to her artistic vision and believes consistency is key to success.

articles.title: Census 2027: Field visits for house-listing, household data collection begin in Jharkhand - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jharkhand began the first phase of its 2027 Census on May 16, 2026.  Trained enumerators will visit homes across the state's 24 districts and 32,459 villages to collect data on housing conditions, family details, and assets. The exercise, which runs until June 14, 2026, has deployed over 76,000 government officers and employees, including field trainers, enumerators, and supervisors.  Jharkhand's Directorate of Census Operations is overseeing the process.

articles.title: A third of Britons believe they have changed social class, survey finds | Class issues | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A survey by Attest found that over a third of Britons identify as belonging to more than one social class, with millennials most likely to do so.  The research also revealed an entrenched sensitivity about class in Britain, with nearly half of respondents feeling judged for their social standing.  Professor Dominic Abrams, director of the Centre for the Study of Group Processes at the University of Kent, believes that traditional class categorizations are less relevant now as people can move between social groups more easily. Nick Harrison, chief executive of the Sutton Trust, highlighted the link between social mobility and happiness, noting that even those who climb the social ladder may not experience equal levels of wellbeing due to factors beyond income.

articles.title: Josef Mengele: Switzerland finally to open secret files on Nazis' Auschwitz 'Angel of Death'
articles.rephrased_article: The Swiss Federal Intelligence Service has agreed to release long-sealed files on Josef Mengele, the notorious Nazi war criminal. The files will be released subject to conditions and requirements yet to be defined.  Historians have long sought access to the files, which contain information about Mengele's possible presence in Switzerland after World War Two, but the Swiss authorities have previously refused requests for their release.  The decision comes after years of debate and legal challenges from historians who argue that the secrecy surrounding the files fuels conspiracy theories. The files are expected to shed light on Mengele's activities during his time in Switzerland, but it remains unclear if they will reveal anything concrete about his presence or actions.

articles.title: LHC upholds widows’ right to interest on delayed insurance payments - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.sentiment_target: State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan
articles.rephrased_article: The Lahore High Court upheld the right of widows and legal heirs of deceased policyholders to receive statutory interest on delayed group insurance payments from State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan. The court rejected the corporation's arguments that Section 47B of the Insurance Act, 1938 was no longer enforceable due to Islamic injunctions. Justice Raheel Kamran dismissed all four appeals filed by the corporation and ordered the payment of statutory interest at a rate five percent higher than the prevailing bank rate from the date of death of each insured person until realization of the amount.  The court also rejected objections regarding limitation and maintainability, noting that the claimants had pursued remedies in good faith despite confusion regarding the proper legal forum for insurance disputes.

articles.title: Meghalaya: Looking beyond the grape | Market demand for fruit wines and an enabling government policy is motivating small-time winemakers to go commercial - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lyang B. Sangma, an entrepreneur from Meghalaya, is excited about the potential of his te.gism fruit wine after it was selected by the Meghalaya Farmers Empowerment Commission (MFEC) to be showcased at Vinexpo India 2024 in Mumbai. The MFEC chose six exotic fruit wines and meads for the event, including Sangma's te.gism product, which has gained recognition from experts and connoisseurs beyond his hometown of Tura.

articles.title: "Erika wanted his position": Candace Owens reacts after Charlie Kirk reportedly named wife Erika as TPUSA successor before assassination
articles.rephrased_article: Charlie Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, allegedly named his wife, Erika Kirk, as the organization's successor in a private donor retreat recording from 2025. The resurfaced audio has sparked online debate and tension surrounding TPUSA's leadership after the board appointed Erika as CEO shortly after Charlie's death. Conservative commentator Candace Owens questioned the authenticity of the recording, demanding its release while TPUSA maintains that donor privacy policies prevent them from sharing recordings from private investor gatherings.

articles.title: Gwadar varsity VC, officials untraceable even after 48 hours - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
