articles.rephrased_article: Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Abdul Razzaq Sabir, Pro-Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Syed Manzoor Ahmed, and two other employees of Gwadar University have been missing since Friday after traveling from Gwadar to Quetta. The group lost contact in the Mastung area, prompting police to believe they may have been abducted. Security forces launched an intelligence-based search operation but no trace of the four individuals has been found. Political and educational circles expressed concern over the situation, urging authorities to ensure their safe recovery.

articles.title: What happened between Benny Johnson and Marjorie Taylor Greene? YouTuber faces grifting accusations during Thomas Massie controversy
articles.rephrased_article: Benny Johnson and Marjorie Taylor Greene engaged in a heated online argument following Greene's reposting of criticism about Johnson's YouTube coverage of allegations against Congressman Thomas Massie.  The dispute began after Johnson discussed accusations from Cynthia West, who alleged that Massie paid hush money during their past relationship. Greene accused Johnson of spreading "lies" and using other people's content, while Massie denied the allegations and called them politically motivated.

articles.title: Lil Tjay sparks backlash after exposing private messages linked to Kai Cenat’s ex-girlfriend
articles.rephrased_article: Lil Tjay sparked backlash after briefly posting screenshots of private messages connected to Kai Cenat’s former girlfriend, Gigi Alayah. The deleted uploads ignited fierce arguments online about whether the rapper crossed a line or simply added another chapter to an ongoing feud.  While some defended Lil Tjay's right to share interactions tied to public tension, many criticized his actions for dragging private conversations into public view. The situation intensified because of previous exchanges between Lil Tjay and Cenat, and fueled speculation about the rapper’s motives for generating online attention.

articles.title: ‘A watchdog without resources is not a watchdog’: Labor accused of letting key accountability body languish | David Pocock | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Labor's budget allocation of $99.8 million for the Australian National Audit Office (ANAO) has been criticized by transparency advocates and independent Senator David Pocock as inadequate, despite warnings from the Parliament’s Joint Committee of Public Accounts and Audit about the agency’s unsustainable financial position.  The funding increase falls below inflation and will result in a decrease in staffing levels at the ANAO, which is tasked with supporting accountability and transparency through independent reporting to parliament. The budget comes amidst concerns that the ANAO may struggle to meet its audit targets due to ongoing funding challenges.

articles.title: California county scam ad lawsuit adds to mounting Meta legal woes | Social Media News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Meta Platforms, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger, and Threads, is facing a new lawsuit from Santa Clara County, California. The county alleges that Meta knowingly profits from scam advertisements, which generated $7 billion in annual revenue, despite claiming to combat them.  The lawsuit claims that Meta's system flags suspected scammers but doesn't ban them unless they are 95% certain of fraud, allowing them to continue running ads for a premium fee. The county argues this practice targets vulnerable consumers and causes financial losses for California residents, particularly seniors.  Meta has denied the allegations, stating that it aggressively fights scams on its platforms and removed 159 million scam advertisements last year.

articles.title: Psychiatrist and writer Anand Nadkarni passes away - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Anand Nadkarni, a psychiatrist and founder of the Institute for Psychological Health in Thane, passed away on May 15, 2026, at the age of 66.  He was diagnosed with a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor in March and underwent multiple surgeries. Dr. Nadkarni dedicated his life to mental health awareness, addiction treatment, literature, and theatre. He founded the IPH in Thane in 1990, which later became an educational center affiliated with several universities.  He also established the Muktangan Addiction Detoxification Centre in Pune. His work was recognized through numerous awards and publications, including his books "Gadhepanchavishi" and "Vishadayoga," which received recognition from the Maharashtra government. Dr. Nadkarni was a prolific writer and contributed to Marathi films and music. He also conducted online and offline mental health awareness activities during the Covid-19 pandemic.

articles.title: Four-year-old boy rescued after falling into borewell in Punjab’s Hoshiarpur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A four-year-old boy, Gurkaran Singh, was rescued after nine hours of an intense operation involving multiple agencies in Punjab's Hoshiarpur district. The incident occurred on Friday night when the child fell into a newly dug borewell at Chak Samana village.  Deputy Commissioner Aashika Jain, Punjab Minister Ravjot Singh, and AAP MP Raj Kumar Chabbewal were present during the operation, which involved teams from the NDRF, SDRF, Punjab Police, fire brigade personnel, and local volunteers. The rescue team created a narrow tunnel to reach the child, who was stabilized after being pulled out of the borewell.  The child's family expressed gratitude to all those involved in the successful rescue.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Galileo Galilei: “There are those who reason well, but they are greatly outnumbered by those who reason badly.”
articles.rephrased_article: Galileo Galilei's quote, "There are those who reason well, but they are greatly outnumbered by those who reason badly," has resurfaced online due to its relevance to the current climate of misinformation and emotional reasoning. The quote reflects a timeless truth about human behavior: that thoughtful reasoning often struggles against the prevalence of irrational thinking, particularly in large groups where emotions drive opinions.  This observation resonates with people today who face constant bombardment of emotionally charged information, making it difficult to discern fact from fiction. Despite its pessimistic tone, the quote offers a glimmer of hope by highlighting that thoughtful questioning and evidence-based reasoning still exist even amidst overwhelming noise.

articles.title: Doe d’oh! Wild deer rescued after escalator escapade in Norwich M&S | Norwich | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A female muntjac deer became trapped upside down in an escalator at a Marks & Spencer department store in Norwich. Wendy Valentine, founder of the Hillside Animal Sanctuary, stated that this was a first for her organization as it is not uncommon for deer to get stuck in various places but never in an escalator.  Ian Haywood, a sanctuary worker, rescued the deer after she became wedged between glass panels and managed to free her with some help from M&S staff. The deer, nicknamed "lucky" Lucy, sustained only a superficial cut on its foot and is now resting at the sanctuary.

articles.title: A plant that “does math”: Scientists uncover hidden Voronoi patterns inside Chinese money plant leaves
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory have discovered that the Chinese money plant, scientifically known as *Pilea peperomioides*, exhibits a hidden mathematical structure resembling a Voronoi diagram. The arrangement of veins and pores within the leaves appears to be organized based on local interactions between cells, creating a complex pattern without any central control or pre-programmed calculations. This spontaneous self-organization suggests that similar principles might govern the development of various biological structures, including those in plants, animals, and even engineering designs.

articles.title: Man hit by van in Birmingham after residents take down union flags put up by anti-migrant group | Birmingham | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police are investigating an incident in Birmingham where a man was run over by a van after a group of people took down union flags put up by the Raise the Colours campaign. The man, in his 30s, suffered a broken leg that required surgery and remains hospitalized. Raise the Colours, a group known for putting up thousands of union and Saint George flags across England, has been criticized for spreading anti-immigrant rhetoric.  West Midlands police are examining CCTV footage and social media to identify the full circumstances of the incident.

articles.title: Meet Zhou Qunfei: Once she worked in a glass factory, now she runs a $26 billion company and sits alongside Elon Musk and Tim Cook at China’s state dinner
articles.rephrased_article: Zhou Qunfei, a self-made entrepreneur, rose from factory worker to founder of Lens Technology, a company valued at $26.6 billion.  Her journey began in rural China where she worked in factories while studying technical skills and eventually launched her own business in Shenzhen specializing in watch glass production.  Lens Technology later became a major supplier for Apple, supplying touchscreen glass for the iPhone and other products. The company expanded its operations to include smart vehicles, AI hardware, robotics, and aerospace manufacturing. Zhou Qunfei's success has made her one of China's richest self-made women.

articles.title: Kadirur panchayat in Kannur bags Atma Nirbhar award - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kadirur grama panchayat in Kannur has been awarded third place nationally for its achievements in the ‘Atma Nirbhar Panchayat Special Award’ category of the National Panchayat Awards 2026. The award recognizes initiatives in poverty alleviation, healthcare, women empowerment, waste management, infrastructure, and good governance.  The panchayat's efforts, including agriculture-based schemes, Kudumbashree activities, and MGNREGS, have significantly reduced poverty levels and strengthened livelihood opportunities. Kadirur has also received recognition for its healthcare network, clean environment initiatives, child-friendly and women-friendly programs, and transparent governance.

articles.title: Super-rich NRI who called himself 'recession-proof' in 2008 sent to jail: His New Jersey mansion had salt water pool surrounded by imported sand
articles.rephrased_article: Parmjit “Paul” Parmar, an Indian-origin investor, has been sentenced to five years in prison for conspiracy to commit securities fraud. Parmar, who previously declared himself recession-proof and boasted a lavish lifestyle, was found guilty of inflating revenues, falsifying bank records, and misleading investors in a publicly traded healthcare services company where he served as CEO. The fraud is estimated to have involved over $212 million.  The scheme, orchestrated by Parmar and others including Sotirios Zaharis, a/k/a “Sam Zaharis,” and Ravi Chivukula, defrauded investors of hundreds of millions of dollars in connection with the funding of a healthcare services company's acquisition.

articles.title: Film industry should avoid wasteful expenditure, but not at the cost of workers, says Kamal Haasan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kamal Haasan, a Rajya Sabha Member and actor, called for changes to the economics of the film industry. He emphasized that these adjustments should not compromise workers' rights or working conditions but instead focus on reducing wasteful practices like excessive travel and inflated production costs. Haasan urged producers, actors, directors, unions, studios, exhibitors, distributors, over-the-top platforms, and guilds to engage in a collaborative conversation to implement more sustainable and efficient film-making practices.

articles.title: Scientists discover ‘shy plant’ that can count without even having a brain
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists at William & Mary, led by Professor Peter Vishton, have discovered that the 'shy plant' (Mimosa pudica) possesses the ability to count events.  In experiments, researchers exposed plants to random light cycles and observed anticipatory leaf-opening behavior depending on the number of cycles they experienced. This suggests that individual cells might learn in complex ways, challenging our understanding of biology and potentially changing how we view plant intelligence.

articles.title: 'No evidence you suffered in India': Inside Sanaullah Khan Mohammed's failed attempt to get asylum in US
articles.rephrased_article: A US Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit denied asylum to Sanaullah Khan Mohammed, an Indian Muslim man who entered the US on a tourist visa in 2016 and overstayed. The court found no merit in his claim of persecution in India, citing that local police intervened in the incident he described and that the slaughterhouse business he claimed was the source of tension is no longer operating.  The court also ruled that Mohammed could be deported to any location within India as it is a large country.

articles.title: CBI launches AI-powered notice verification system ‘Abhay’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has launched an AI-based helpbot called “Abhay” to authenticate CBI notices and combat cyber fraud. The agency stated that cyber-enabled fraud is a growing problem in India's criminal justice system, exacerbated by advancements in technologies like artificial intelligence.  Citizens can access Abhay through the CBI’s official website at www.cbi.gov.in.

articles.title: Chud the Builder visibly disappointed as bond hits $1.25 million
articles.rephrased_article: Chud the Builder, whose real name is Dalton Eatherly, appeared upset in court after a judge set a $1.25 million bond for him on Friday in Tennessee. The streamer faces several charges related to a shooting outside a courthouse, including attempted murder and aggravated assault.  The judge scheduled more hearings for next month before Chud was escorted back into custody. His reaction to the large bond amount has sparked online discussion about the case's strange details and whether he acted in self-defense.

articles.title: Erling Haaland to make film acting debut – as a Viking called Haaland | Movies | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Erling Haaland, the Manchester City striker, will make his acting debut in the animated film "Viqueens".  The film, directed by Harald Zwart, features Haaland as an animated version of himself and follows two Viking girls who travel to China. Zwart believes Haaland's global icon status makes him a perfect fit for the story. The film is slated for release around Christmas.

articles.title: 50 Green Card holders identified to be deported as US starts re-vetting older cases
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Homeland Security has established a new unit, the "Tactical Operations Division," to re-vet Green Card applications. The unit, headed by Daniel Andrade, has identified at least 50 individuals through its review process and found that 80% of those cases were clean, requiring no further action.  Experts argue that this exercise is meaningless as Green Cards are already subject to extensive vetting. However, the unit can potentially lead to deportation for those convicted of crimes or who obtained their status fraudulently.

articles.title: ICE releases wife of US soldier and Afghanistan veteran from detention
articles.rephrased_article: ICE released the wife of a US Army sergeant and Afghanistan veteran, Deisy Rivera Ortega, from detention after she was arrested for immigration violations.  Rivera Ortega had been detained while applying for parole-in-place status with her husband, Sgt Jose Serrano, who is a US citizen by birth. Senator Tammy Duckworth, an Illinois Democrat and Iraq War veteran, called Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to express concern over the detention. The couple's case highlights concerns about ICE's treatment of military spouses and raises questions about its handling of immigration cases.

articles.title: Czech police find stolen skull of medieval saint encased in concrete | Czechia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Saint Zdislava, a 800-year-old relic believed to be the skull of the saint, was recovered encased in concrete after being stolen from a Czech church. A 35-year-old man confessed to stealing the relic and planned to throw it into a river before his arrest by police in Mladá Boleslav on Thursday. The suspect, who has no prior criminal record, faces up to eight years in prison if convicted.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Michelle Obama: “When someone is cruel or acts like a bully, you don’t stoop to their level. No, our motto is…”
articles.rephrased_article: Michelle Obama’s famous quote, “When someone is cruel or acts like a bully, you don’t stoop to their level. No, our motto is, ‘When they go low, we go high,’” gained popularity after being spoken at the 2016 Democratic National Convention.  The phrase quickly spread beyond politics and became part of everyday conversation due to its relatable message about responding to cruelty with dignity. The quote resonates because it addresses a universal human experience: dealing with difficult interactions in a way that maintains one's own integrity, even when faced with provocation. This sentiment is particularly relevant in today’s online culture, where negativity often thrives.  The phrase offers a reminder of the importance of emotional restraint and self-control, especially during times of conflict.

articles.title: Thousands in black robes with doubtful degrees: CJI Kant - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant criticized what he called "attacks on the judiciary" by media, social media, and RTI activists during a hearing regarding an advocate's plea for contempt proceedings over alleged delay in implementing senior advocate guidelines. The Bench, also comprising Joymalya Bagchi, dismissed the petition, stating that senior advocate designation is not a status symbol but a distinction conferred by the court.  The court expressed concern over fake law degrees and urged the CBI to investigate.

articles.title: ‘Half of British Muslims are under 25’: Report shows shifting demographics | Demographics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A new report by the Muslim Council of Britain reveals that British Muslims are one of the youngest and fastest-growing groups in the country, with nearly half under 25. The report highlights this demographic shift as potentially shaping future political battles, particularly if the voting age is lowered to 16.  The study also emphasizes the diverse nature of British Muslim communities, ranging from Pakistani communities in Bradford to Somali communities in Cardiff. While acknowledging challenges like lone-parent families and lower home ownership rates, researchers emphasize that British Muslims are increasingly educated, entrepreneurial, and engaged citizens. The report concludes by questioning whether Britain's institutions are prepared for the scale of demographic change already underway.

articles.title: Chandran Pillai steps down as GCDA Chairperson - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Chandran Pillai, former Chairperson of the Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA), resigned following a change in state leadership.  He highlighted achievements including revitalized projects, new interventions, and a long-term urban planning vision, citing the "Bodhi" urban development conclave as key to this transformation.  Pillai emphasized land pooling as a model for future development, particularly for Infopark's third phase.

articles.title: Deputy Chairman Pranesh writes to Chikkamagaluru SP to take back escort vehicle - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council, M.K. Pranesh, has requested the withdrawal of his official escort vehicle in response to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for austerity measures.  Pranesh, who represents local bodies in Chikkamagaluru, stated he was voluntarily giving up the vehicle as a way to reduce fuel consumption and contribute to national efforts to conserve resources.

articles.title: 68pc of passwords can be cracked within a day: report - Tech - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A cybersecurity report by Kaspersky analyzed 231 million leaked passwords between 2023 and 2026, revealing alarming patterns. The vast majority of compromised passwords either begin or end with digits, making them vulnerable to brute-force attacks.  The report also found that commonly used symbols like '@' and '.' are frequently overused, while emotional words and trending phrases are often employed as password bases. Alexey Antonov, Data Science Team Lead at Kaspersky, recommends using less common characters and avoiding predictable patterns for stronger passwords.

articles.title: Lawmakers decry slow internet in National Assembly, across country - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Several members of the National Assembly raised concerns about slow internet connectivity affecting the paperless working environment in parliament.  Deputy Speaker Ghulam Mustafa Shah directed authorities to address the issue, while Federal Information Technology and Telecom Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja assured them that the spectrum auction would improve internet facilities. Khawaja also addressed concerns over digital harassment, online fraud, and data theft, emphasizing public awareness campaigns and collaboration with relevant institutions.

articles.title: Purple Line metro services to be suspended for two hours on May 17 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) announced that train services on the Purple Line between Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Station and Sir M. Visvesvaraya Station, Central College will be suspended from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. on Sunday for essential maintenance work.  Metro operations on other stretches of the Purple Line will continue as usual during this disruption period. The affected section is expected to resume normal service at 9 a.m.

articles.title: Fact check: Did Chud The Builder post racist Facebook updates after courthouse shooting? Viral screenshot debunked
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton “ChudTheBuilder” Eatherly, a 28-year-old streamer, was arrested after a shooting outside the Montgomery County Courthouse in Clarksville, Tennessee.  A screenshot claiming to show a Facebook post from Eatherly defending his actions with racist language and mocking the injured man began circulating online. However, authorities confirmed that the post is fake and there is no evidence of it being written by Eatherly. The incident resulted in both men suffering gunshot wounds and being taken to hospitals. Sheriff John Fuson stated that violence will not be tolerated and that those responsible will be held accountable.

articles.title: US hotel owners expected a World Cup boom - so far it hasn't happened
articles.rephrased_article: Despite widespread anticipation and marketing efforts, US hotel owners are reporting lower than expected bookings for the World Cup. The American Hotel and Lodging Association (AHLA) found that eight in 10 hotels in host cities are experiencing decreased demand compared to last year, with many describing the tournament as a "non-event."  The association attributes some of this decline to factors like the political climate, rising living costs, and high ticket prices. Airbnb has predicted the World Cup will be its biggest hosting event yet. While some fans remain optimistic about the tournament's impact on local businesses, concerns persist over ticket pricing and visa application processes.  The White House has established a taskforce to ensure smooth operations for the event.

articles.title: Supreme Court allows actor Darshan to revive bail plea in a year if no ‘substantial progress’ in trial - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court expressed disappointment over the slow pace of the trial in the 2024 Renukaswamy murder case involving Kannada actor Darshan Thoogudeepa. The court granted him liberty to renew his bail plea if there is no "substantial progress" within a year, directing the trial court to ensure regular witness examinations and avoid adjournments on flimsy grounds.  The top court also directed prison authorities to provide Mr. Darshan with basic amenities as per jail manual rules and for the Karnataka High Court to address the issue of the vacant presiding officer position at the trial court.

articles.title: One interaction cannot be viewed in isolation, says PPP's Shazia Marri after Bilawal's mid-presser curtness - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari was criticized for his curtness with Shazia Marri, a spokesperson for the party, during a press conference. The incident occurred after Das, Minister of State for Religious Affairs and Interfaith Harmony, suggested that the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) be devolved to provinces.  Marri addressed the situation on X, stating that the interaction should not be viewed in isolation, emphasizing the PPP's commitment to public service. Digital rights expert Usama Khilji and think tank executive director Imtiaz Gul condemned the incident, calling it misogynistic and disrespectful.

articles.title: The humility habit: Why Bill Gates and Warren Buffett voluntarily swapped the boardroom for a fast food counter
articles.rephrased_article: Bill Gates and Warren Buffett, the world's richest men, participated in a fast-food job experience at a Dairy Queen branch as part of a Berkshire Hathaway shareholder weekend. This unusual experience allowed them to gain firsthand knowledge of customer service operations by learning to use cash registers, take orders, and handle customer interactions.  By stepping outside their usual corporate environment, they learned the importance of proximity to front-line work in understanding real challenges and making informed decisions.

articles.title: Giggle v Tickle: Australia court increases payout for trans woman in landmark discrimination case
articles.rephrased_article: A Sydney court doubled the discrimination payout for an Australian trans woman, Roxanne Tickle, who was removed from a female-only app. The Federal Court dismissed an appeal by the app's founder, Sall Grover, finding that Grover engaged in direct discrimination against Tickle based on her gender identity.  The court also found that the original judge erred by not deeming Tickle's removal as direct discrimination.  Grover intends to appeal the decision to the High Court.

articles.title: Scientists identify massive new dinosaur following Thailand dig | Science and Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists from University College London have identified a new species of dinosaur, Nagatitan chaiyaphumensis, in Thailand.  This massive herbivore is estimated to have weighed as much as nine adult elephants and stretched 27 meters long. The newly discovered sauropod is believed to have roamed the region between 100 and 120 million years ago, making it the largest ever found in Southeast Asia. Researchers believe Nagatitan was a bulk browser that consumed large quantities of vegetation.  The discovery adds to the growing list of known dinosaur species from Thailand, bringing the total number to 14.

articles.title: Watch: Inside Vijay’s ‘Leo’-inspired cafe in Kashmir - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sifar Cafe in Anantnag district, Kashmir, has seen a surge in tourists from Tamil Nadu, India following the assumption of office by new Chief Minister Vijay. The cafe is the location where Vijay's 2023 film "Leo" was filmed.  Visitors are recreating scenes and ordering "chocolate coffee," a popular item featured in the movie.

articles.title: Adani Group: Gautam Adani, nephew Sagar to pay $18m to settle civil fraud case in the US
articles.rephrased_article: Gautam Adani and his nephew, Sagar Adani, have agreed to pay $18 million to settle a civil fraud lawsuit filed by the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The 2024 lawsuit accused them of paying bribes to Indian officials for renewable energy projects and misleading US investors about anti-bribery practices.  The proposed agreement, which does not admit or deny the allegations, also bars the Adanis from future violations of key US anti-fraud laws.

articles.title: Giggle for Girls app discriminated against trans woman Roxanne Tickle, appeal judge rules when doubling damages | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The federal court upheld a landmark decision that found the women-only social media app, Giggle for Girls, and its founder, Sall Grover, unlawfully discriminated against Roxanne Tickle based on her gender identity. The court awarded Tickle $20,000 in damages after finding she was directly discriminated against twice when excluded from accessing the app.  The decision affirms that transgender women are protected under the Sex Discrimination Act and sets a precedent for future cases involving discrimination based on gender identity.

articles.title: How Tagore’s songs were ahead of their time in form and feeling - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: To celebrate the 165th birth anniversary of Rabindranath Tagore, a professor at Jadavpur University urged students to explore his musical oeuvre.  Tagore's songs, according to experts like Reba Som, offer a unique synthesis of words, tones, and melody, encompassing a wide range of emotions and themes.  His work has been praised by prominent figures such as W.B. Yeats and Ritwik Ghatak, who saw its enduring power and relevance to the human experience.

articles.title: From drab partitions to haute couture host: how a Sydney civic masterpiece was rescued | Culture | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Lands building in Sydney, once a grand sandstone masterpiece and hub for land administration, has been transformed into a high-end lifestyle and cultural precinct.  A team led by Hassell and Purcell Architecture, won the top heritage award for their meticulous restoration project that revealed original features like grand staircases and vaulted ceilings. The building, which served as the engine room of New South Wales’ colonial expansion, will be home to luxury retail, dining, and event spaces when completed later this year.  The project also received recognition for its scale and impact on Sydney's cultural landscape.

articles.title: Vellore Corporation installs free drinking water points at 20 spots for public during summer - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Vellore Corporation has installed free drinking water points at 20 locations within its limits to assist residents, especially vulnerable groups like women and senior citizens, during the ongoing summer heat wave. The initiative aims to provide access to clean water in crowded public areas such as markets and bus terminals. Each zone will have at least four water points, with each tank holding an average of 1,000 liters of water.  The water supply will be replenished every two days, and the civic body is monitoring the distribution points to prevent misuse for commercial purposes. The project was delayed due to election-related restrictions but will remain operational until June-end.

articles.title: Who is Empath Chan? Controversial streamer shuts down viral death rumors with blunt response
articles.rephrased_article: Empath Chan, a controversial online personality, refuted rumors of her death from a drug overdose after a parody account called DissidentWire falsely reported it. The rumor spread quickly across social media despite the account's history of satirical content.  Chan responded with a simple message: "? I’m alive," which went viral and highlighted the ease with which fake news can spread online, especially concerning controversial figures.

articles.title: Who is Chud the Builder? Controversial creator Dalton Eatherly linked to viral chaos and Tennessee shooting investigation
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton Eatherly, known online as "Chud the Builder," is facing renewed scrutiny after investigators linked him to a shooting incident outside the Montgomery County Courthouse in Clarksville, Tennessee. The incident resulted in injuries to two people and has reignited debate about internet fame built on shock content.  While authorities continue their investigation, critics are questioning whether internet creators who thrive on outrage and provocation are contributing to dangerous real-world behavior.

articles.title: "Why did the military prioritize Erika": Candace Owens claims Erika Kirk’s emotional WHCD shooting clip was strategically amplified
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens has accused the White House Military Office of manipulating public sentiment surrounding the White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting by circulating an internal email encouraging officials to amplify a video of Erika Kirk leaving the ballroom visibly shaken.  Owens claims the email described the footage as having "the strongest emotional-response asset associated with the incident" and that it was mistakenly shared with the wrong groups before attempts were made to delete it. No official evidence has been released, and authorities have not verified Owens' claims.

articles.title: Kochi Corpn.’s Fort Queen ferry to get a new lease of life - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kochi Corporation has proposed an estimated ₹27.29 lakh for the dry dock of its passenger boat, the Fort Queen, to revive its service. The corporation plans to reintroduce the boat as a temporary option during ro-ro vessel service gaps and is exploring partnering with the Kochi Metro Rail Limited.  However, Kerala Shipping and Inland Navigation Corporation Ltd. (KSINC) claims the boat was withdrawn due to safety concerns and viability issues, citing low daily earnings and logistical challenges. The corporation will also discuss renewing the boat's agreement and insurance at its upcoming council meeting.

articles.title: High-stakes courtroom drama of Musk v OpenAI hears closing arguments | OpenAI | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Closing arguments concluded in Elon Musk's lawsuit against Sam Altman and OpenAI, with both sides presenting their cases.  Musk's attorney, Steven Molo, argued that Altman is untrustworthy and that the company's restructuring into a for-profit entity was a breach of their founding agreement. OpenAI's attorneys countered that Musk is motivated by jealousy and that the company has always remained committed to its non-profit mission. The jury will now deliberate on whether they believe Altman and OpenAI are liable, with potential consequences for the company's future as it seeks a public listing.

articles.title: Kick streamer Clavicular’s jaw hammering confession takes unexpected turn after revealing life with multiple girlfriends
articles.rephrased_article: Clavicular, a social media personality, sparked online discussion after revealing his past habit of hitting his jaw with a hammer during his teenage years. He claimed the practice was motivated by a belief it could alter his facial shape. The conversation also touched upon Clavicular's current dating life, stating he is seeing three women and plans to add another soon.  The interview has generated strong reactions online, with many questioning the seriousness of his claims.

articles.title: The trillion-dollar asteroid: NASA is chasing an asteroid that contains more gold than exists on Earth
articles.rephrased_article: NASA's Psyche mission, launched in 2023, is focused on studying the metal-rich asteroid 16 Psyche. The asteroid, discovered in 1852, is believed to be the exposed core of an ancient planet and could offer insights into how planets like Earth formed billions of years ago.  The spacecraft will orbit Psyche and study its composition, magnetic field, gravity, surface geology, and internal structure. While headlines often focus on the asteroid's potential monetary value, scientists are primarily interested in what it reveals about planetary formation and the development of metallic cores.

articles.title: NSPCC reports sharp rise in children being blackmailed over sexual images in UK | Children | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The NSPCC reported a 36% increase in contacts with its Childline service related to online sexual abuse and exploitation last year, driven by an increase in blackmail cases. The most common forms of blackmail involved financial “sextortion,” threats using AI-generated explicit images from children's phones, and forced sharing of new explicit images. MPs on the science, innovation and technology committee have called for stronger social media regulations, including age limits and transparency on algorithms.  The government is currently consulting on various measures to improve online safety for children, including an Australian-style under-16 age limit for accessing social media.

articles.title: Closing arguments begin in Elon Musk’s landmark lawsuit against OpenAI | Elon Musk News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Elon Musk and his lawyer, Steven Molo, accused OpenAI, its CEO Sam Altman, and president Greg Brockman of breaching their charitable trust by prioritizing profit over AI safety.  Molo argued that Altman is untrustworthy and that OpenAI enriched investors at the expense of its nonprofit mission. OpenAI's lawyers countered, claiming Musk waited too long to file his lawsuit and that he himself wanted to turn OpenAI into a for-profit company. The case hinges on whether the lawsuit was filed within the statute of limitations and whether OpenAI had a "charitable trust".

articles.title: Delhi court orders OpIndia to remove articles on Swati Chaturvedi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Delhi court ordered OpIndia to remove two articles about journalist Swati Chaturvedi, citing potential harm to her reputation while the defamation suit is pending.  The court found that the source articles did not support the claims against Ms. Chaturvedi and accepted her argument that many alleged defamatory statements could not be linked to public domain information. The judge noted that Ms. Chaturvedi's professional reputation is crucial, and temporary removal of the articles would not prejudice OpIndia's ability to present their case during trial.

articles.title: From searching for stars to finding Wi-Fi: The failed radar experiment that changed the world
articles.rephrased_article: A team of Australian radio astronomers from the CSIRO in the late 1970s conducted a failed experiment to detect exploding black holes.  Instead, they developed mathematical techniques using the Fast Fourier Transform to filter out cosmic noise and mitigate multipath interference. This breakthrough proved crucial for high-speed indoor networking technologies like Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. The technology, originally intended for scientific research, has become essential for global connectivity and digital communication.

articles.title: Renowned feminist artist and film-maker Valie Export dies aged 85 | Austria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Valie Export, the Austrian performance artist and filmmaker, died at age 85 in Vienna.  Known for her provocative performances that challenged patriarchal power structures, she is considered a pioneer of feminist art. Export's work, which included the controversial "Tapp und Tastkino" (Tap and Touch Cinema) where she exposed the objectification of women, continues to influence contemporary artists. Her legacy will be remembered through exhibitions like the 1980 Venice Biennale, where she co-exhibited with Maria Lassnig.  Her work is celebrated by institutions worldwide, including a dedicated center in Linz, Austria.

articles.title: “We no longer have free speech”: Sneako compares Chud the Builder backlash to Charlie Kirk debate after shocking Tennessee arrest case
articles.rephrased_article: Sneako, a livestreamer, expressed concern that the arrest of Dalton Eatherly, also known as Chud the Builder, could signal a decline in free speech rights in America.  He argued that people are becoming too quick to punish even words without considering constitutional protections. The shooting incident at the Montgomery County Courthouse in Clarksville, Tennessee, led to charges against Eatherly for attempted murder and other offenses. Authorities confirmed both men involved were in stable condition after the incident.

articles.title: American poet Sasha Debevec-McKenney wins Dylan Thomas prize for ‘blistering’ debut poetry collection | Dylan Thomas prize | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sasha Debevec-McKenney, an American poet, won the Dylan Thomas Prize for her debut poetry collection, "Joy Is My Middle Name". The £20,000 prize was awarded to writers aged 39 or under in honor of the Welsh poet Dylan Thomas.  The judges praised the collection as “an exuberant, blistering collection full of life, humor and ideas” and noted its unique voice that feels like an antidote to current times. Debevec-McKenney's work explores themes of race, addiction, womanhood, and consumerism, resonating with a generation of readers who relate to her experiences.

articles.title: CBI conducts searches in Reliance Communications case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) conducted searches at seven premises linked to former executives of Reliance Communications Limited (RCom) in Mumbai, Gurugram, and Bengaluru. The searches are part of ongoing investigations into alleged fraud cases involving Rs 27,337 crore reported by various Public Sector Banks and LIC. These investigations stem from the last few months when the CBI registered seven cases against the Anil Ambani-led Reliance Group.

articles.title: Meet Grigori Perelman: The math genius who solved a 100-year-old problem and rejected a $1 million prize and the Fields Medal
articles.rephrased_article: Grigori Perelman, a Russian mathematician, solved the century-old Poincaré Conjecture, one of mathematics' most challenging problems. He achieved this feat by building upon earlier work from mathematician Richard S. Hamilton and published his proof online in 2002 and 2003.  Despite being awarded the Fields Medal in 2006, Perelman refused both the honor and a $1 million prize offered by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2010. He chose to live a quiet life away from public attention, rejecting fame and recognition for his work.

articles.title: 5 massive pyramids still standing today: Why the largest one is not in Egypt
articles.rephrased_article: The Great Pyramid of Cholula, located in Puebla, Mexico, is considered the world's largest pyramid by volume.  This massive structure, constructed over centuries by various Mesoamerican cultures, covers an immense base area of 450 by 450 meters and dwarfs other ancient pyramids like the Great Pyramid of Giza in size. While the Great Pyramid of Giza is known for its height, the Cholula pyramid's volume makes it the true global leader.  However, accurately measuring these ancient structures remains a challenge due to erosion, collapse, and scavenging.

articles.title: Scientists say SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket will strike the Moon at 5,400 miles per hour
articles.rephrased_article: A spent SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage, part of the Blue Ghost Mission 1, is scheduled to crash into the Moon on August 5, 2026. The four-ton object, traveling at high speed, will impact near the Einstein crater's edge.  The event highlights concerns about space debris between Earth and the Moon and provides an opportunity for scientists to study the resulting crater and lunar soil movement. The Minor Planet Centre and orbital trackers identified the object as 2025-010D. The Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee (IADC) suggests disposing of such stages in heliocentric orbits to prevent future crashes.

articles.title: US reportedly dropped fraud charges against Indian billionaire after he hired Trump’s lawyer | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Justice has dropped fraud charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani after he hired a new legal team led by Donald Trump's personal lawyer, Robert J Giuffra Jr.  Giuffra presented a plan for Adani to invest $10 billion in the US economy and create 15,000 jobs if the charges were dropped. Prosecutors stated that the potential investment wouldn't sway their decision, but one official found it favorable. Adani was accused of bribing Indian officials and misleading investors with false statements.

articles.title: Yale medical school discriminated against Asian and White applicants, claims Trump administration
articles.rephrased_article: The Justice Department concluded a year-long investigation into the admissions practices at Yale School of Medicine, finding that its leadership intentionally discriminated against White and Asian applicants in favor of Black and Hispanic students. The department's findings, detailed in a letter from Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon, revealed that Yale used "holistic reviews" to assess applicants' race through direct and indirect means, ultimately violating federal law prohibiting race-based admissions.  The investigation also found no change in racial preferences despite the Supreme Court ruling that allowed for consideration of factors beyond test scores.

articles.title: 'We didn't die': Pilot recounts crash landing in Atlantic off Florida coast
articles.rephrased_article: Ian Nixon, a Bahamian pilot, and ten passengers were forced to ditch their plane in the Atlantic Ocean after experiencing multiple engine failures during a routine flight.  The aircraft landed roughly 175 miles north of Miami, prompting a last-resort ditching maneuver. Capt Rory Whipple, a member of the US Air Force's 920th Rescue Wing, and Maj Elizabeth Piowaty responded to an emergency locator transmitter signal and rescued all eleven passengers from the life raft after hours of waiting.  The passengers were transported to a Florida hospital where three suffered minor injuries. The Bahamian authorities are investigating the cause of the crash.

articles.title: Australia news live: Delta Goodrem hits the stage in Eurovision semi; Angus Taylor accused of ‘dog whistle’ budget reply | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Delta Goodrem performed her song "Eclipse" in the second semi-final of Eurovision before Sunday's final. Angus Taylor, the Opposition leader, claimed migrants were accessing welfare payments immediately upon arrival but advocates for migrants refuted this claim, stating that there are lengthy wait periods for most Centrelink payments.  The Coalition government plans to tie migration levels to housing construction and has not specified which migrant categories would be cut.

articles.title: Quote of the day by German philosopher Walter Benjamin: “In the end, we get older, we kill everyone who loves us through the worries we give them, through the troubled tenderness we inspire in them, and the fears we ceaselessly cause.”
articles.rephrased_article: Walter Benjamin's quote, "In the end, we get older, we kill everyone who loves us through the worries we give them, through the troubled tenderness we inspire in them, and the fears we ceaselessly cause," captures the emotional weight of deep human connection.  The quote reflects the anxieties inherent in loving deeply, acknowledging that caring for another person inevitably brings worry, fear, and exhaustion. While Benjamin's words are melancholic, they highlight the enduring power of love and its inevitable consequences. This sentiment resonates with readers today because it speaks to the emotional vulnerability that comes with genuine attachment, a truth often obscured by idealized portrayals of relationships in modern society.

articles.title: Karachi's Shahrah-i-Bhutto to be fully open to public by end of May: Sharjeel Memon - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Memon announced the full opening of the Shahrah-i-Bhutto Expressway in Karachi by the end of May, a 39-kilometer high-speed corridor that will connect to the M-9 highway.  Memon stated the project is expected to save commuters at least an hour traveling into the city and improve traffic flow. Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah had previously directed for full operationalization by April 2026. Additionally, Memon announced a new road connecting Karachi Port with the Taj Haider Bridge, which will be completed around the same time as the expressway's opening.  Memon highlighted that these projects are part of a larger effort to improve connectivity and convenience in Karachi.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Mahatma Gandhi: “In prayer it is better to have a heart without words than words without a heart.”
articles.rephrased_article: Mahatma Gandhi’s quote, "In prayer it is better to have a heart without words than words without a heart," resonates with modern audiences because it emphasizes the importance of genuine emotion over polished expression. The quote acknowledges that while many people communicate through carefully crafted words and social media posts, emotional honesty often feels more authentic and trustworthy.  This sentiment speaks to the human desire for sincerity in relationships and interactions, especially amidst an increasingly performative culture.

articles.title: Tasmac shuts 150 outlets in three days; salesmen face challenges from customers - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation Limited
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has ordered the closure of over 150 liquor outlets in Tamil Nadu, citing proximity to educational institutions and places of worship. The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation Limited (Tasmac) is responsible for identifying and closing these shops based on multiple criteria, including distance from public spaces and average sales figures.  The government has also issued a circular warning against selling liquor above the Maximum Retail Price (MRP), with officials instructed to conduct surprise inspections across the state.

articles.title: 3 things OPT employers should check as ICE announces crackdown on 10,000 foreign students
articles.rephrased_article: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) announced a crackdown on foreign students participating in the Optional Practical Training program, uncovering widespread fraud involving fake companies and non-existent work sites. Emily Neumann, an immigration attorney, advises companies to verify their Form I-983s, ensure supervisors are aware of training responsibilities, and report terminations within five business days. ICE found empty buildings, residential addresses listed as work sites, coordinated employer clusters, and a single owner operating multiple entities to evade taxes and obscure employment relationships.

articles.title: Giant new dinosaur identified from remains found in Thailand
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists from the UK and Thailand have identified a new type of giant long-necked dinosaur, nicknamed "the last titan" of Thailand.  The Nagatitan chaiyaphumensis, weighing 27 tonnes and measuring 27 meters in length, lived between 100 and 120 million years ago during a period when atmospheric carbon dioxide levels were rising. The discovery sheds light on how ancient climatic conditions allowed for the development of gigantic dinosaurs.  The study was published in Scientific Reports journal.

articles.title: Florida crew recounts ‘miraculous’ Atlantic plane rescue with fuel low | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Military rescue crews from the 920th rescue wing at Patrick Space Force base in Florida successfully rescued all 11 passengers and crew members of a crashed Beechcraft twin-propeller aircraft after it ditched into the Atlantic Ocean. The survivors, all Bahamian adults, had been clinging to a small life raft for about five hours before being airlifted to safety by Combat King II transport plane and HH-60W Jolly Green II helicopter.  The rescue operation was hampered by choppy seas and an incoming thunderstorm, with the last survivor hoisted aboard just as the helicopter's fuel ran out.

articles.title: Who was Pedro Ballester? UK student on path to becoming Catholic Church’s first Gen Z saint
articles.rephrased_article: The Roman Catholic Diocese of Salford has officially opened the cause for the beatification and canonization of Pedro Ballester, a Manchester student who died from cancer at age 21. The process, which involves an investigation into Ballester's life, writings, and reputation for holiness, will now invite people with personal knowledge of him to submit letters, diaries, and memories.  The opening of the cause marks the first formal step towards sainthood for Ballester, who was associated with Opus Dei and known for his commitment to religious life and service.

articles.title: 'You are doing nonsense': Indian man counters Texas whistleblower Sara Gonzales over H-1B allegation, calls her jobless
articles.rephrased_article: Sara Gonzales, a Texas journalist, targeted Great America Technologies for alleged H-1B fraud in her latest video.  The confrontation between Gonzales and the company's director, Nagarjuna Reddy Sakam, escalated into an altercation with Sakam claiming his business is legitimate and not engaging in illegal activities.  Sakam threatened legal action against Gonzales for what he perceived as harassment and trespassing.  James Blunt, a US entrepreneur who frequently comments on immigration issues, reviewed the company's operations and found no wrongdoing.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Banksy: “I mean, they say you die twice. One time when you stop breathing and a second time, a bit later on, when somebody says your name for the last time.”
articles.rephrased_article: Banksy’s quote, “I mean, they say you die twice. One time when you stop breathing and a second time, a bit later on, when somebody says your name for the last time,” has resonated widely online due to its simple yet profound exploration of mortality and memory.  The quote's conversational tone and understated emotional impact make it relatable and enduring, prompting reflection on the lasting impact of human connection and the fragility of our existence. Despite the digital age's emphasis on permanence, this quote highlights the impermanence of online fame and the importance of personal connections in shaping a meaningful legacy.

articles.title: Air India inflicts $743 million hit on Singapore Airlines, dragging FY26 profit down 57% - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Singapore Airlines reported a 57.4% decline in full-year net profit to $930 million (SGD $1.18 billion) for the fiscal year 2025-26, primarily due to Air India's losses. The Tata Group carrier's stake in the merged Air India-Vistara entity contributed a $743 million (SGD 945.2 million) hit to Singapore Airlines' bottom line.  This marks the first full year that Singapore Airlines has absorbed the impact of Air India's losses after acquiring its stake in November 2024.

articles.title: 400 employees became millionaires overnight when a founder sold his startup for $3.7 billion before its IPO
articles.rephrased_article: Jyoti Bansal, founder of software company AppDynamics, sold the company to Cisco in 2017 for $3.7 billion, transforming the lives of nearly 400 employees into millionaires overnight.  Bansal considered various factors before accepting the offer, including financial valuation, integration with Cisco's business, and potential market volatility. While he acknowledged the emotional impact of selling his company, Bansal prioritized employee well-being and believed the acquisition was the best decision for AppDynamics at the time. Bansal later co-founded software companies Harness and Traceable, demonstrating his continued influence in the startup world.

articles.title: James Dyson: Why James Dyson kept building prototypes long after most people would quit? This reveals his billionaire invention rule | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: James Dyson, founder of the Dyson company, developed his bagless vacuum cleaner through 5,127 prototypes.  His perseverance and iterative design process demonstrate that successful inventions often result from a long series of testing, failure, and correction rather than sudden inspiration. This approach is now widely recognized as crucial in product development, with companies like National Institute of Standards and Technology recognizing the benefits of prototype testing for improving product quality.

articles.title: MoS Arjun Ram Meghwal takes e-rickshaw ride in Rajasthan’s Bikaner to promote fuel conservation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Arjun Ram Meghwal, Union Minister of State for Law and Justice, traveled to his residence in Bikaner by e-rickshaw on Thursday to promote fuel conservation.  He joined Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call for austerity measures amidst global energy crises. Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma has also reduced the number of vehicles in his convoy.

articles.title: One dead and two fighting for their lives after bus rolled off road in Whitsundays region | Queensland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A coach carrying 29 people rolled on the Bruce Highway in Gumlu, Queensland, resulting in one fatality and multiple critical injuries.  Emergency services responded to the scene, with eleven ambulances, two helicopters, and a Royal Flying Doctor Service plane attending. The driver escaped with minor injuries, and the road was closed in both directions. Queensland police are investigating how the crash occurred.

articles.title: Modern antisemitism built on old Jewish stereotypes and tropes, royal commission told | Royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Dave Rich, the Community Security Trust’s policy director, testified before the royal commission into antisemitism and social cohesion that modern-day antisemitism has evolved from traditional tropes found in documents like the Protocols of the Elders of Zion. Rich explained that these negative stereotypes about Jewish people, often rooted in historical accusations such as blood libel or claims of being Christ killers, persist today and are frequently used to justify violence against Jews. He emphasized the need for governments to define antisemitism to combat it effectively while acknowledging the complexities of determining when criticism of Israel crosses into antisemitic territory.

articles.title: He started Dave’s Hot Chicken with $900: Years later, 19 employees became millionaires after a $1 billion deal | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Graham Walker, founder of Fibrebond Corp., reportedly shared $240 million with 540 employees following the sale to Eaton. Similarly,  Dave's Hot Chicken CEO Bill Phelps rewarded 19 employees with millions after a $1 billion investment deal by Roark Capital. This move sparked conversations about employee loyalty and how companies reward their workforce. These examples challenge traditional corporate practices that often prioritize shareholder returns over employee compensation.

articles.title: 50 years of Annakili: The film that launched Ilaiyaraaja’s career
articles.rephrased_article: Ilaiyaraaja, whose career was launched by the film "Annakili,"  shared a close bond with Gangai Amaran, who worked on the soundtrack and provided rhythm guitar for the movie. Amaran recalled how the high notes in the song "Annakili Unnai Theduthey" foreshadowed Ilaiyaraaja's future success.

articles.title: ‘Stunned and shocked’: Ingrid Horrocks wins top prize at New Zealand’s Ockham awards for her fiction debut | New Zealand | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ingrid Horrocks, a Wellington-based poet and memoirist, won the prestigious Jann Medlicott Acorn prize for fiction at the 2026 Ockham New Zealand book awards for her debut short story collection, "All Her Lives." The book follows nine women across different life stages and generations as they navigate politics, gender, and motherhood.  Horrocks' win marks only the fifth time a short story collection has won the top prize since the awards began 58 years ago. Craig Cliff, a fiction judge, praised Horrocks' "crisp, clear, and unencumbered" writing style and her ability to tackle different perspectives of womanhood.
